S08-002 · 1. The thesis

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

1. The thesis

Everything needed for a world-class local-first + realtime platform already exists across these repos — as parts. What is missing is one cohesive contract that makes the parts compose: a single per-target data-plane matrix, a single sync topology with clearly separated read/write/presence paths, one extension component model shared by client and server (instead of two WIT dialects), one settings/schema surface that extensions declare and containers store-and-sync, and one packaging + distribution standard with signing. The KnowMe Builder skill set then becomes the authoring harness: skills that let AI tools create, test, sign, publish, and install these extensions against the standard.

The rest of this document specifies each of those five contracts.

S08-003 · 2. Per-target data plane (the ground truth to build on)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Explicit amendments:
  • Mobile presentation is native Flutter; shared Rust semantics remain. See RT-01–11.

2. Per-target data plane (the ground truth to build on)

Hard constraints already verified in docs/pglite-oxide-tauri-hybrid.md — the spec must not fight them:

Tier Local store How Sync client
Web (all browsers) PGlite idb:// (+ relaxedDurability), OPFS-AHP where Chrome/Firefox-only is acceptable WASM in a worker; live extension for reactivity frf-wasm (pub/sub, CRDT, agent) + Electric shapes
Desktop (Tauri: macOS/Win/Linux) pglite-oxide (PGlite WASI guest in a Rust host, real PG wire protocol) — SQLx/SeaORM unchanged Rust core sidecar; falls back to PGlite-in-WebView if the sidecar is undesirable frf-sdk-rust in the Tauri core
Mobile (iOS/Android) SQLite + sqlite-vec (iOS cannot run Postgres: no fork, no JIT) via gen_ui_core FFI (already the POC pattern) uniffi FFI transport (Swift/Kotlin/Dart bindings exist in FRF)
Cloud Postgres 18 via flint-forge Quarry REST/GraphQL under RLS; Anvil in-DB compute FRF CDC (frf-postgres-cdc) feeds the spine

Consequences the spec embraces rather than papers over:

  1. "Same SQL everywhere" holds for web/desktop/cloud, not mobile. The entity layer — @prometheus-ags/prometheus-entity-management (Zustand/React) and its Flutter/Riverpod counterpart — is therefore the portability boundary, not SQL. Repositories beneath the entity graph speak PGlite SQL on web/desktop and SQLite SQL on mobile; everything above (stores, hooks/providers, components) is dialect-free.
  2. PGlite has no RLS. Tenancy is enforced at the shape factory (predicates ⊆ server RLS), exactly as electricsql-tenant.ts in prometheus-entity-management already does. That invariant becomes normative in this spec (§4.3) and extends to extensions: an extension can never attach a shape without a tenant predicate.
  3. Schema discipline: server tables = client tables + _local columns; additive-only migrations, versioned, applied at boot; divergent local models go in a client_* namespace. Extensions get a namespaced schema each (§5.4).

S08-004 · 3. Sync topology — three paths, not one

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3. Sync topology — three paths, not one

The single biggest architecture failure mode in local-first systems is forcing all data through one sync mechanism. The evidence across the field guide and FRF's design says: separate three paths with different consistency needs.

S08-005 · 3.1 Read path — replicated queries (server-authoritative)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.1 Read path — replicated queries (server-authoritative)

Postgres (flint-forge) → CDC → shapes → local store. Two interchangeable engines:

  • ElectricSQL shapes into PGlite (web/desktop) — the field guide's recommended default; partial replication by predicate, TCC+ consistency.
  • FRF EntityService watch as the sovereign alternative: Quarry's FLINT_CHANGE_SOURCE=fabric already anticipates this; the missing WatchEntityType RPC in FRF is a known gap (it currently fails closed) and is a P0 item in the plan (§8, W1). This gives one spine for entity replication that mobile (no Electric client) can also consume over FFI.

Rule: the read path is rebuildable state. Blowing away the local replica and re-syncing must always be safe.

S08-006 · 3.2 Write path — intent log (client-authoritative until acked)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.2 Write path — intent log (client-authoritative until acked)

Local writes are recorded as idempotent, keyed actions in the local DB (_local write-tracking columns + an outbox table), pushed over FRF Spine (durable Iggy log), applied server-side through Quarry/Anvil under RLS, and confirmed back through the read path. Retry-with-poison + dead-letter for non-idempotent effects (field guide §6 policy, adopted normatively). This is also exactly the shape of knowme_ofp's Hand/run sync in the KnowMe spec — OFP becomes a profile of this path (§3.5).

S08-007 · 3.3 Collaboration/presence path — CRDT (peer-authoritative)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.3 Collaboration/presence path — CRDT (peer-authoritative)

Document-style and presence state (cursors, co-editing, agent scratchpads, settings, per §6) does not belong in either path above. It rides Loro CRDTs via frf-crdt (LoroDeltaApplier) with deltas fanned out over:

  • FRF Sync service (server-relayed, durable) — default;
  • WebRTC data channels (str0m signaling is already proven in FRF phase 18) for P2P/offline-LAN merge;
  • lora-rs as a constrained transport profile for off-grid deltas — must be treated as a delta budget problem (LoRa duty-cycle + payload limits ⇒ compressed, batched, priority-tiered deltas; presence never rides LoRa). This is a research question for the incoming report: recommended framing is "CRDT delta scheduling under transport budget", not "sync over LoRa".

S08-008 · 3.4 Why this triad is the recommendation

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.4 Why this triad is the recommendation

Server-authoritative replication for queryable data (fast, tenant-safe, rebuildable); logged intents for writes (auditable, offline-safe, idempotent); CRDTs only where multi-writer merge is the actual requirement. Zero/LiveStore-style "CRDT everything" systems buy simplicity at the cost of RLS/tenancy and Postgres compatibility — the wrong trade given flint-forge's Anvil/RLS investment. PowerSync/RxDB only matter if Postgres were not the backend; it is.

S08-009 · 3.5 OFP alignment

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Explicit amendments:
  • Key control does not establish reverse-DNS namespace ownership; separate registry proof is required.

3.5 OFP alignment

KnowMe's OFP (FUNC-SPEC §07, rust/crates/knowme_ofp) is this topology restricted to a personal mesh: EntityService-style replication for Hands/conversations, intent log for runs, Loro for memory-graph merge, did:key: payload encryption, mTLS peers. The spec should declare OFP an FRF profile (same proto, personal-peer deployment) rather than a parallel protocol — one codebase, two deployment shapes (BossFang peer vs. flint gateway).

S08-010 · 4. Agents: client-side and cloud-hosted, one contract

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4. Agents: client-side and cloud-hosted, one contract

  • Client-side agents — UAR/gen_ui_agent (desktop/mobile via FFI; browser via frf-wasm::agent) run against local models and the local data plane; skill calls Cedar-governed; outputs written as ordinary intents (§3.2) so they sync like any write.
  • Cloud agents — Kiln edge functions (fke-runtime) and BossFang/librefang instances run against Quarry + Anvil (including in-DB LLM via Flint Ember); they publish results onto the Spine, arriving at clients through the read path.
  • The contract: frf-agentproto ContentBlock is already the wire shape for agent traffic; adopt it as the single agent-event vocabulary and map AG-UI events onto it (§5.3). An agent is then location-transparent: the same Hand definition (knowme_hands::HandDefinition) deploys to a device, a BossFang peer, or a Kiln function — deployment target changes latency and capability, never the protocol.

S08-011 · 5. The extension component model (the heart of this spec)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5. The extension component model (the heart of this spec)

S08-012 · 5.1 Unify the two WIT worlds

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5.1 Unify the two WIT worlds

Today there are two adjacent contracts: knowme:plugin@0.1.0 (client container, rust/crates/knowme_plugin_host/wit/) and flint:host@0.1.0 (Kiln edge functions, flint-forge/wit/ + flint-skill SDK). Same substrate (Wasmtime + Component Model), overlapping host surfaces (log, storage/kv, invoke, events vs. db, llm, kv, identity, secrets). Proposal: factor a layered family under one package namespace:

prometheus:component/core@0.1.0      log, kv-storage, emit-event, clock        (every host)
prometheus:component/agent@0.1.0     uar-invoke (Cedar-gated skills)           (client + Kiln)
prometheus:component/data@0.1.0      sql-query (scoped schema), entity-graph   (per §5.4)
prometheus:component/llm@0.1.0       complete, embed (local model or Ember)    (capability-gated)
prometheus:component/ui@0.1.0        render surfaces (per §5.3)                (client containers)
prometheus:component/settings@0.1.0  schema declaration + change notification  (per §6)

A native skill is a component exporting the skill world (today's Kiln/UAR shape). A full extension is a component exporting skill + ui + settings worlds. Hosts advertise which interfaces they provide; the installer refuses a component whose imports exceed the host's surface — capability negotiation is structural, at install time, before any code runs (same posture as KnowMe FUNC-SPEC §08).

S08-013 · 5.2 What a full extension can add

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5.2 What a full extension can add

Per the requirement: (a) native skills for agent harnesses; (b) UI/UX surfaces; (c) a settings schema the container stores and syncs; (d) entity types with sync policies; (e) Hands templates; (f) scheduled/event handlers. All declared in the manifest (§7.2), all reviewed at install.

S08-015 · 5.4 Extension data: scoped schemas with sync policies

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5.4 Extension data: scoped schemas with sync policies

Each extension gets a namespaced schema (ext_<id> on Postgres; same-named tables in PGlite/SQLite). The manifest declares each table's sync class: replicated (read-path shape, tenant predicate mandatory — shape-factory invariant applies), intent (outbox), crdt (Loro doc), or local-only. Migrations ship in the package, additive-only, applied by the container at install/upgrade — client-side by the container runtime, server-side through a Quarry admin surface. Anvil's flint_meta reflection makes the server side introspectable; the same metadata drives client codegen.

S08-016 · 6. The common settings model

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6. The common settings model

Settings are the first proving ground for the whole stack, because they exercise every layer at small scale:

  • Extension declares a JSON-Schema (2020-12) settings document in its manifest (settings.schema.json) plus per-field metadata: scope (device | user | tenant), sync class (default: crdt for user scope, local-only for device scope, replicated for tenant scope), sensitivity (secret fields route to keychain/Vault, never CRDT).
  • Container renders the settings UI generically from schema (React and Flutter renderers; A2UI form components) — extensions get a settings page for free; both desktop/src/features/settings and mobile/lib/features/settings grow one dynamic panel, not N.
  • Values live in the container store (Zustand slice / Riverpod provider) backed by a Loro map per (extension, scope); synced per §3.3 (FRF Sync, WebRTC, or OFP mesh); server persistence lands in ext_<id>._settings via the intent path when tenant-scoped.
  • Change notification enters the component through settings@0.1.0 (on-change(key, value-json)), so extensions react live on every device.

This model is exactly KnowMe FUNC-SPEC §07's "Settings: default per-device" made precise: scope decides sync, schema decides rendering, sensitivity decides storage.

S08-017 · 7. Packaging & distribution

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7. Packaging & distribution

S08-018 · 7.1 Position

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Explicit amendments:
  • Key control does not establish reverse-DNS namespace ownership; separate registry proof is required.

7.1 Position

Do not invent a new decentralized VCS. Compose three proven layers, all already present or trivially reachable from flint-forge:

  1. Content addressing & transport: IPFS (KnowMe FUNC-SPEC §08 already commits to CID install + gateway fallback; fke-store-ipfs exists) and OCI registries (fke-store-oci) as the enterprise mirror — the same artifact, two transports.
  2. Signing & identity: dual-path exactly as Kiln already implements — fke-sign-did (Ed25519 over canonical manifest, publisher did:key: — the sovereign path, matches KnowMe's plugin trust model verbatim) and fke-sign-cosign (Sigstore/cosign — the enterprise/supply-chain path, works with OCI + Rekor transparency log).
  3. Versioning & discovery ("the git-like part"): a signed, append-only release log per extension (name → ordered list of (version, CID, manifest hash, signature)), itself a CRDT/merkle log that syncs over the same fabric — publishable to IPNS/DNSLink, an OCI tag list, or a plain git repo of manifests. Evaluate Radicle (Rust, sound-theory decentralized git) in the research report as the collaboration/source layer; but the distribution unit is the signed component artifact, not the repo.

S08-019 · 7.2 The package format (`.pxt` — prometheus extension)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.2 The package format (.pxt — prometheus extension)

An IPFS/OCI directory: manifest.json (extends knowme_plugin_host::PluginManifest: id, version, WIT worlds imported/exported, permissions, uar_skill_allowlist, settings schema ref, ui surfaces, entity schemas + sync classes, migrations, signature block), component.wasm, migrations/, ui/ (optional HTMX/A2UI assets), settings.schema.json, SBOM.spdx.json. SHA-256 of every file in the manifest; manifest signed per §7.1.2. Version semantics: 0.x minor = breaking (as knowme:plugin already states); hosts pin world versions.

S08-020 · 8. What to add, where (project plan skeleton)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8. What to add, where (project plan skeleton)

Workstreams, orderable after the research report confirms §3–§7:

  • W1 — FRF gap: implement WatchEntityType RPC (unblocks Quarry FLINT_CHANGE_SOURCE=fabric and the sovereign read path). Small, unlocks the most.
  • W2 — WIT family: factor prometheus:component/* worlds from flint:host@0.1.0 + knowme:plugin@0.1.0; adapters so existing Kiln skills and KnowMe plugins keep working; publish flint-skill-style authoring SDKs (Rust first, TS/Go via componentize).
  • W3 — Container runtime (this repo): extend knowme_plugin_host M3 scope to the full extension model — settings engine (schema→UI renderers for React + Flutter), extension event router (HTMX + AG-UI paths), scoped-schema migrator over PGlite/SQLite.
  • W4 — Data plane adapters: pglite-oxide provider in gen_ui_db for Tauri; PGlite worker + entity-graph wiring for web; sqlite-vec parity layer for mobile; outbox/intent tables + retry-with-poison runtime as a shared crate (prometheus-sync-core), used by both knowme_ofp and web/desktop clients.
  • W5 — CRDT settings + collaboration: Loro-backed settings maps end-to-end (FRF Sync → WebRTC fallback); the LoRa delta-budget spike (research-gated).
  • W6 — Packaging: .pxt format + forge-cli/new pxt CLI verbs (init, build, sign [did|cosign], pin [ipfs|oci], publish-log, install, verify); registry log format.
  • W7 — KnowMe Builder skills: new skills in the two skill repos that drive W2–W6 with AI harnesses: pxt-new-extension, pxt-settings-schema, pxt-ui-surface (HTMX and A2UI variants), pxt-entity-schema, pxt-test-harness (golden tests against a containerized host), pxt-sign-and-publish, pxt-install-verify; wire them into orchestrate-prometheus-application and the openspec-* change workflow so extension development is itself spec-driven.
  • W8 — Conformance: a host-conformance suite (does a container correctly enforce permissions, shape predicates, settings scopes?) — this is what makes "conform to our standard" testable, and what the AI skills run in CI.

S08-021 · 9. Questions the deep-research report must settle

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

9. Questions the deep-research report must settle

  1. Electric shapes vs. FRF EntityService as the primary read path (or Electric on web-only, FRF everywhere else)? Cost of running Electric alongside the fabric?
  2. Loro vs. Automerge/Yjs stance is settled by frf-crdt (Loro) — but confirm Loro's Dart/FFI story for Flutter parity, and snapshot/compaction strategy for years-long settings histories.
  3. TanStack DB's role vs. entity-graph-react at scale (field guide decision #7).
  4. LoRa: realistic delta budgets (SF/duty cycle), and whether meshtastic-style store-and- forward is worth a transport adapter, or LoRa should be deferred entirely.
  5. Radicle vs. plain signed-manifest git repos vs. IPNS for the release log; petname/ naming layer for extension discovery.
  6. WASI 0.2/0.3 timeline effects on the component worlds (async exports would simplify handle-event streaming).
  7. Precedents worth mining for the extension UI sandbox: Figma plugin iframe model, Zed extensions, Obsidian, VS Code webviews — what do they get wrong that the A2UI-as-data path avoids?
  8. Settings-as-CRDT prior art (e.g., Ditto, Jazz, Instant) — anything to steal for scope semantics and secret-field handling?

S08-022 · 10. Recommendation (pre-report)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10. Recommendation (pre-report)

Adopt the triad sync topology (§3) with flint-forge as the sole server datastore and FRF as the sole spine; unify the WIT surfaces into prometheus:component/* (§5.1) so one signed component runs as a Kiln edge function, a KnowMe client extension, or both; make settings the first end-to-end vertical (§6); package as .pxt over IPFS+OCI with DID+cosign dual signing (§7); and grow the KnowMe Builder skill set into the authoring harness (W7) so every one of these artifacts is producible, testable, and publishable by an AI agent under the openspec workflow. Nothing here requires new infrastructure categories — every layer extends a crate or skill that already exists in these repos.

S18-001 · Plugin Strategy — A Capability-Centric Open Model

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Explicit amendments:

Plugin Strategy — A Capability-Centric Open Model

AMENDMENT — 2026-08-04 (v1.4). Amended by uar-plugin-system-research-2026-08-04.md (this directory; canonical copy in universal-agent-runtime/docs/plugins/). Authoritative deltas over this document wherever they conflict:

  • Ownership split. The plugin contract layer (WIT family uar:plugin@0.2.0, host interfaces seeded near-verbatim from librefang:plugin@0.1.0, capability-card schema, manifest+signing, lifecycle, shared sandbox host crate, and the runtime-generic recognized set renamed uar:agent/uar:tool/uar:skill/uar:hook/uar:provider/ uar:entity-schema/uar:settings) is owned and published by the Universal Agent Runtime. This document remains authoritative for the KnowMe product layer: knowme:* product capabilities (knowme:theme, app-shell chrome, Hands binding), marketplace + entitlement VC issuance, trust pills, sharing/distribution UX, and settings-form product behavior. Governance follows the A2UI precedent: UAR owns the contract; KnowMe is the named reference implementation driving amendments.
  • Host profiles. headless vs full-ui conformance profiles are first-class; capability cards declare profile_required and installers reject mechanically.
  • Card schema v2 additions: profile_required, combination_risk (risky permission combinations surfaced at install), namespace_proof (did:web/DNS-TXT or transparency-log receipt — did:key alone does not prevent reverse-DNS squatting).
  • Settings schema: JSON Schema 2020-12 is the single version (§11 stands; the companion plan's draft-7 references are superseded).
  • Security fixes now normative (research doc SR-1…SR-12): signed advisory/revocation blocklist + auto-quarantine, host-stamped event provenance with emit-allowlist and rate caps, contributor reentrancy guard, generations/rollback, crash-loop circuit breaker, universal action I/O validation, and honest mobile execution budgets (iOS = Pulley interpretation; no .cwasm on iOS).

Scope: the plugin system as a wide-open capability vocabulary: what a capability is, the recognized set we publish, how plugins declare (or invent) capabilities, A2UI component libraries as the cross-platform UI plane, headless plugins, discovery/matching/routing via embedded capability cards, and the decisions we lock in now so a marketplace can exist later.

Status: v1.0 strategy, 2026-07-18. Supersedes the "plugin kinds" framing in docs/knowme-builder-extensibility-spec.md §5 (which becomes the transport layer for this model) and completes docs/strategies/agents/README.md §4: a native agent is a plugin carrying the agent capability — nothing more. Companions: docs/strategies/model-configuration/README.md (resolver used by callbacks), docs/knowme-functional-spec.html §08 (trust/distribution base).

S18-002 · 1. The inversion

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

1. The inversion

The previous framing enumerated extension kinds (skill, UI surface, settings, agent). This document inverts it:

We publish a vocabulary of capabilities. A plugin is a signed WASM package that declares which capabilities it provides — one, many, or ones we've never heard of.

Consequences, in order of importance:

  1. Agents are not special. "Native agent" = a plugin declaring knowme:agent. Same manifest, same signing, same sandbox, same installer, same audit. (The Hands wizard remains the product surface that binds an agent-capability plugin into a Hand — see agents doc §4.3.)
  2. The system is open at the vocabulary level. Third parties can invent capabilities we haven't defined. Recognized capabilities get first-class treatment; unrecognized ones are carried, sandboxed, and discoverable — their ecosystems give them meaning (§5).
  3. Anything is expressible: an agent, a skill pack, a CRM connector, a theme, a settings-only integration, a streaming filter, a UI component library, a data-type provider — or combinations, in one package.

S18-003 · 2. The capability declaration ("capability card")

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2. The capability declaration ("capability card")

Every capability — recognized or invented — is declared with the same card shape. Recognized ones live in the signed capability registry (published alongside the model catalog, same Ed25519 discipline); invented ones ship only in the plugin's manifest.

{
  "id": "knowme:agent",                 // namespaced; reverse-DNS for third-party
  "version": "0.1.0",                   // 0.x semver: minor = breaking
  "name": "Agent",
  "description": "Autonomous task executor with A2A-style lifecycle …",
  //   ^ name+description+tags are the EMBEDDABLE text — vectorized locally into the
  //     capability index for search, matching, and routing (§7)
  "tags": ["agent", "automation", "a2a"],

  "settings_schema": { "$ref": "…" },   // JSON Schema 2020-12; rendered by the generic
                                        // settings engine; scopes per extensibility spec §6
  "actions": [                          // A2A-style tasks this capability exposes
    { "id": "start-task", "input_schema": {…}, "output_schema": {…},
      "streaming": true, "description": "…" }
  ],
  "events": {                           // bus topics, namespaced by capability id
    "emits":    [ { "topic": "task-status", "payload_schema": {…} } ],
    "consumes": [ { "topic": "knowme:context/assembled", "optional": true } ]
  },
  "chunks": [                           // stream-chunk types handled during hook
    "text-delta", "tool-call", "thinking", "a2ui-patch",
    { "id": "com.acme.chart-frame", "schema": {…} }        // custom chunk kinds allowed
  ],
  "ui": {                               // OPTIONAL — §4; absence = headless
    "a2ui_components": [ { "id": "task-board", "schema": {…},
                           "actions": ["start-task"], "events": ["task-status"] } ]
  },
  "requires":  [ "knowme:kv@0.1" ],     // capability dependencies (host must provide)
  "enhances":  [ "knowme:agent@0.1" ]   // optional composition: adds to another
                                        // capability's surface when both are present
}

requires/enhances are cheap now and load-bearing later: they are how a plugin extends another plugin without a new mechanism.

S18-004 · 3. The recognized set (v0.1)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3. The recognized set (v0.1)

Published, schema'd, first-class in UI and routing. Deliberately short; grown by evidence, per the same restraint the WIT contract already practices:

Capability What declaring it means
knowme:agent A2A-shaped task lifecycle (agents doc §4); bindable into Hands; carries its own identity (§9)
knowme:tool A single MCP-compatible callable: name, description, JSON-Schema input/output, annotations — the atomic spec-first unit (see strategies/skill-support)
knowme:skill A packaged practice: one or more tools + instructions + policy defaults + settings, with a scope (global / agent-private / agent-exposed) — see strategies/skill-support
knowme:hook Declared participation in named pipeline stages (agents doc §3)
knowme:provider An LLM/embedding provider kind + settings schema (model-config doc §2.2)
knowme:ui-library A2UI component library (§4), no behavior of its own
knowme:entity-schema Namespaced tables + sync classes (extensibility spec §5.4)
knowme:settings Settings-only integration (config that other capabilities read)
knowme:theme Design-token pack within the brand system's constraint envelope

A plugin declares any subset. A "full extension" in the old framing is just skill + ui-library + settings + entity-schema in one package.

S18-006 · 4.1 Why this is structurally correct (not just convenient)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.1 Why this is structurally correct (not just convenient)

The WASM sandbox already forbids platform code, so UI must cross the boundary as data; A2UI makes that constraint a feature. Compared to the iframe/webview model (Figma plugins, VS Code webviews): no per-plugin web runtime, no style divergence (plugins inherit design tokens and accessibility from the renderer and cannot go off-brand — the theme envelope is enforced by construction, not by review), and the security model collapses to "the component vocabulary is the sandbox" — no DOM access, no script injection surface. The deeper win: agent-generated UI and plugin UI are one pipeline — one renderer pair, three producers (app, agents, plugins) — which no webview approach can offer.

S18-007 · 4.2 The four disciplines this stands on

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.2 The four disciplines this stands on

A2UI succeeds or fails on execution of exactly four things:

  1. Vocabulary governance with an honest ceiling. The component vocabulary is versioned registry data, like capabilities: additions ship as schema + renderer updates on evidence of demand, never ad hoc. The expressiveness wall is planned for, not denied: a rich standard library first; declarative escape hatches next (e.g. a chart component that takes a spec, not a drawing surface); and the webview/HTMX path retained only as an audited exception (§4.3). Unknown components degrade gracefully: renderers below a plugin's declared vocabulary minimum render a labeled fallback, never a crash or a blank.
  2. Renderer parity as a tested contract. One schema source of truth generates both renderers' types; a conformance suite of golden renderings runs on both platforms per vocabulary version (the flutter-golden-ui harness skill covers half of this today); divergence is a bug class with an owner, not a known quirk. If parity is an intention rather than a gate, Flutter becomes the second-class citizen within a year.
  3. Local interaction semantics. Components are deliberately stateful where interaction demands it: inputs with local echo, declarative validation, optimistic toggles. The bus sees debounced semantic events ("field committed", "form submitted"), never raw keystrokes. This is the difference between SDUI that feels native and SDUI that feels like a survey iframe — and it also keeps the audited bus signal-dense instead of noise-flooded.
  4. Authoring experience, or no ecosystem. Ships with the vocabulary, not after it: a hot-reloading A2UI playground fed by a running plugin, side-by-side React/Flutter preview, and a pxt-ui-surface Builder skill that scaffolds components and screenshots both renderers into the plugin's docs. Nobody builds for a UI system they can't see.

S18-008 · 4.3 The HTMX/webview path is an exception, not an alternative

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.3 The HTMX/webview path is an exception, not an alternative

Demoted explicitly: two first-class UI systems would fork the ecosystem and double the conformance budget. A capability may declare a webview/HTMX surface only with a ui-escape-hatch permission — amber at install, listed in the posture audit, and carrying its own sandbox terms (isolated webview, no host bridge beyond the standard invoke/subscribe). The expectation named in the card's review UI: escape-hatch surfaces are web/desktop-only and second-class on mobile. Every escape-hatch grant is a data point for what the A2UI vocabulary is missing — reviewed when considering vocabulary additions (§4.2.1).

S18-009 · 5. Headless plugins and the open vocabulary

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Explicit amendments:
  • Key control does not establish reverse-DNS namespace ownership; separate registry proof is required.

5. Headless plugins and the open vocabulary

  • No UI required, ever. A capability + events is a complete plugin (a silent CRM sync, a log enricher, a webhook bridge). The installer and library UI treat headless as normal, not as "missing UI."
  • Unrecognized capabilities are carried intact: permissions still declared and enforced, sandbox identical, events namespaced under the capability id, settings schema still rendered generically (it's just JSON Schema). What they don't get: structured pipeline stages (hooks require recognized knowme:hook declarations), first-class product surfaces, or our schema validation of their action payloads. UI: a neutral unrecognized pill (distinct from trust pills — a signed plugin can carry unrecognized capabilities; the two axes are independent).
  • Name integrity: reverse-DNS ids + publisher did:key: signatures prevent squatting; the registry will refuse recognized-namespace (knowme:*) declarations from unsigned or non-first-party publishers.
  • Promotion path: an invented capability that gains ecosystem traction can be adopted into the recognized registry (with its incumbent implementations grandfathered) — the vocabulary is versioned data, so recognition is a registry publish, not an app release.

S18-010 · 6. Manifest v2 (`.pxt`)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Explicit amendments:
  • Key control does not establish reverse-DNS namespace ownership; separate registry proof is required.

6. Manifest v2 (.pxt)

The extensibility spec's manifest gains capabilities: [CapabilityCard] and retires per-kind fields. Unchanged: content addressing (IPFS/OCI), SHA-256 per file, Ed25519 / did:key: signing, permission review at install, SBOM. Added now — dormant until the marketplace (§8): publisher (stable DID), license (SPDX or commercial ref), and an optional entitlement block (verification endpoint + public key) that v1 hosts ignore.

S18-011 · 7. Discovery, matching, routing

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7. Discovery, matching, routing

Capability cards are text, so they index like everything else:

  • Local capability index — on install, the device embeds each capability's name/description/tags + action descriptions with the device's own index binding (model-config doc §6 rules apply: the index stamps its embedding model+dim; registry ships canonical text, never vectors — precomputed vectors would break the moment a user changes embedding models).
  • Routing — the route pipeline stage queries this index: "user intent looks like com.acme.crm-sync's import-contacts action" arrives as a scored routing contribution, same provenance/budget discipline as any hook contribution. Unrecognized capabilities participate in this semantic matching fully; only structured stage participation is gated on recognized declarations.
  • Marketplace search later = the same index server-side over the registry's published cards. One mechanism, two deployments.

S18-012 · 8. Marketplace-later (what we lock in now)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Explicit amendments:
  • Key control does not establish reverse-DNS namespace ownership; separate registry proof is required.

8. Marketplace-later (what we lock in now)

Business model explicitly deferred — critical mass first; distribution stays open, free, and sideload-friendly. But three things are cheap now and expensive to retrofit, so they land in manifest v2 immediately:

  1. Stable publisher identity — the signing did:key: is the merchant identity later; key rotation gets a documented procedure now.
  2. License + entitlement fields — schema'd, ignored by v1 hosts. The entitlement standard is W3C Verifiable Credentials (Data Model 2.0, SD-JWT/JOSE securing): the trust plane is already DID-native on both ends — publishers sign manifests with did:key (issuer), users hold did:key identity keys (holder) — so a paid entitlement is a VC: issuer = author DID, subject = user DID, claims = {plugin_id, tier, version_range, type: perpetual|subscription|trial|seat, expiry}. Properties this buys: - Offline, sovereign verification — pure signature-chain checking in the container; no license server, works air-gapped (stronger than the license-key → presigned-URL sketch in local-models §5.2, which remains the download-gating transport; the VC is the rights object). - Wallet sync for free — a VC is a small signed document; it syncs over OFP as a user-scoped entity, so every instance's identity keystore is the wallet and rights are presentable on any device without re-authentication. - Enforcement at install/update/activation, never runtime — Cedar evaluates the entitlement claim in the activation policy; a lapsed subscription blocks updates, never bricks installed software. - Revocation by lifetime, not lists — perpetual = long-lived VC, no revocation (sold stays sold); subscription = short-lived VC (30–90 d) reissued on renewal; Bitstring Status List available as an issuer-optional online freshness check. Transfer/resale = reissuance under author policy, never bearer passing. Teams = issue to org DID; members present membership + org entitlement as a delegation chain through the existing org/personal Cedar layering. - Honesty clause — client-side verification is friction-for-honesty, not DRM; the paid value is signed authenticity, updates, support, and convenience. No arms race. - One credential shape for everything — Pro-tier licensed models, team memberships, and future feature entitlements are the same VC with different claim types: one wallet, one verifier, one Cedar integration.
  3. Review-ready metadata — SBOM, permission declarations, and capability cards are exactly what a curated storefront needs to render listings and diff permission changes across versions. No extra work later; it's the same artifact.

Revenue split, curation policy, refunds: out of scope until traction.

S18-013 · 9. Governance and identity

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Explicit amendments:
  • Key control does not establish reverse-DNS namespace ownership; separate registry proof is required.

9. Governance and identity

Governance is part of the specification, not an afterthought bolted on at install:

  • Every capability card may carry a governance block: Cedar policy templates (the plugin's proposed defaults, rendered and reviewed at install exactly like permissions), resource budgets (tokens, invocations/hour, network destinations), and the data classes touched. The host merges these proposals with the user's policies; the plugin never grants itself anything.
  • Agents are principals. Each agent instance — a deployed Hand, whether declarative or component-backed — is minted its own did:key: at creation and registered with the container (and, when server-connected, with the identity plane: Ory/flint-gate). Identity is per-instance, never per-definition: two installations of the same shared agent are two principals.
  • Dual-identity resolution. Every governed action carries user as subject and agent as actor — the RFC 8693 token-exchange pattern. Server-side, flint-gate issues short-lived JWTs with sub = user, act = agent DID, plus claims: capability set, hand id, placement, policy version. Because flint_auth (Anvil) already injects JWT claims into Postgres GUCs, RLS can natively distinguish "the user directly" from "the user via agent X" — no new database machinery. Locally, Cedar evaluates with the agent as principal and the user in context; policies may require either or both ("Inbox Triage may read mail for Travis; nothing may send mail").
  • Audit keys on the pair. Every audit-trail entry records (user, agent, capability, action) — the question "what did this agent do on my behalf" becomes a query, and revoking one agent's access never touches the user's own.

S18-014 · 10. Sharing

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10. Sharing

Plugins, agents, Hands, and skills are sharable artifacts — they are signed text and WASM, so sharing is distribution, not replication of authority:

  • Channels: OFP peers (personal mesh, team instances), signed export bundles, or published .pxt CIDs — same trust pipeline regardless of channel.
  • Definitions travel; identity and grants do not. A received agent is installed like any plugin: fresh agent DID, permission review, first-use consent, its proposed Cedar policy shown as a proposal. A shared artifact can never carry its author's authority into your system.
  • Team semantics ride the team instance: an org publishes governed agents/skills to its BossFang; members install with org Cedar policies layered over personal ones (org policy can forbid what personal policy would allow, never the reverse).

S18-015 · 11. The settings substrate

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

11. The settings substrate

Everything in this ecosystem has settings — plugins, capabilities, agents, skills, tools, indexes — and all of it stores in one metadata-driven substrate (aligned with the prometheus-entity-management metadata base-schema approach): two tables, JSON columns, schema-as-data.

-- identical shape in SurrealDB (client) and Postgres/flint-forge (server)
settings_definition(
  id, owner_kind,            -- capability | plugin | agent | index | container
  owner_id, key,
  schema JSONB,              -- JSON Schema 2020-12
  scope,                     -- device | user | tenant | agent
  sensitivity,               -- normal | secret (secret ⇒ keychain/Vault ref, never value)
  sync_class, version, ui_hints JSONB )

settings_value(
  definition_id,
  scope_key,                 -- e.g. user:did:… | device:… | tenant:… | agent:did:…
  value JSONB,               -- validated against schema at write
  clock JSONB,               -- CRDT/Lamport metadata for synced scopes
  updated_at, updated_by )   -- updated_by is a (user, agent) pair — §9 audit rule

Consequences: one generic settings engine validates, stores, syncs (per scope and sync class), and audits every setting in the system regardless of complexity; A2UI settings components are generated from schema + ui_hints — every plugin gets a settings page on every platform for free, and a plugin may optionally ship custom A2UI components for richer settings UX, bound to the same definitions; the agent scope is the fourth scope — agent instances have their own settings resolved through the same tables; migrations are additive schema-version bumps on the definition row, with old values migrated lazily by the engine. Secrets are references into keychain/Flint Vault — the substrate never holds secret material, so the tables sync freely under their declared sync classes.

S18-016 · 12. Open questions (defaults taken, flagged for decision)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

12. Open questions (defaults taken, flagged for decision)

  1. Card embedding ownership — default: registry ships text, devices embed locally (taken in §7). Alternative rejected: registry-shipped vectors.
  2. Unrecognized capabilities in routing — default: semantic matching yes, structured stages no (taken in §7). Revisit if it proves too conservative.
  3. enhances composition semantics — v0.1 limits it to additive surface (extra actions/components on the target capability); no interception of the target's traffic. Interception, if ever, needs its own threat model.
  4. Chunk-type governance — custom chunk kinds are namespaced and schema'd, but who renders an unknown chunk? Default: hosts drop unknown chunks silently except into consumers that declared them. Confirm.

  5. knowme:theme envelope — resolved (v1.1): the envelope is enforced by construction (§4.1) — plugin UI renders only through the token-bound A2UI renderers, so a theme capability can only rebind tokens within the design system's constraint schema (single-accent restraint encoded as a validator on the token set); it can never inject styling past the renderer.

  6. Agent JWT lifetime & refresh — default: short-lived (≤15 min) actor tokens issued per run by the placement's gateway; long-running tasks refresh via the placement, never hold long-lived credentials. Confirm against flint-gate's token model.

  7. Org-over-personal policy layering (§10) — restrictive-only merge is the default; confirm no legitimate case requires an org grant exceeding personal policy.
  8. Entitlement-VC issuance topology — author-issued directly, marketplace as co-issuer/broker (revenue split needs the marketplace in the flow), or both? Default: schema supports either issuer; topology decided with the marketplace. Related: author key rotation/compromise procedure for the issuer DID must be documented before any paid issuance begins.

S18-017 · 13. Implementation map (this repo)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

13. Implementation map (this repo)

  • rust/crates/knowme_plugin_host: CapabilityCard types + manifest v2 parsing; capability registry fetch/verify; per-capability WIT world binding (agent world per agents doc §4.1, skill/hook worlds per extensibility spec §5.1).
  • gen_ui_agent: routing-stage query against the capability index; event bus topic namespacing by capability id.
  • gen_ui_db_graph: capability index tables with {model_ref, dim} stamps.
  • gen_ui renderers (React + Flutter): A2UI component registration from ui-library cards; a2ui-patch chunk handling in the stream renderer.
  • Registry publishing job: capability registry as a second signed document beside the model catalog, same origin (local-models doc §5.2).
  • Identity: agent-DID minting in knowme_hands (creation flow); actor-token issuance in the sidecar/BossFang gateway (flint-gate RFC 8693 exchange); flint_auth claim mapping for the act claim; Cedar entity schema gains the agent principal type.
  • Settings substrate: settings_definition/settings_value repositories in gen_ui_db (SurrealDB) and a matching flint-forge migration; generic validation + scope resolution in one Rust module shared via FFI/WASM; A2UI settings-form generator in the gen_ui renderers.
  • Docs cross-updates: agents doc §4.3 notes agents-are-plugins (done); skills/tools split defined in docs/strategies/skill-support/README.md; extensibility spec §5 re-scoped as transport under this vocabulary at next revision.

S19-001 · KnowMe Universal Plugin System — Recommendation, Architecture, Functional Specification & Project Plan

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

KnowMe Universal Plugin System — Recommendation, Architecture, Functional Specification & Project Plan

AMENDMENT — 2026-08-04 (v1.1, authoritative deltas). This plan is amended by uar-plugin-system-research-2026-08-04.md (this directory; canonical copy in universal-agent-runtime/docs/plugins/). The following supersede the corresponding sections below wherever they conflict:

  1. Contract ownership moved to UAR. The plugin contract (WIT family, host interfaces, capability-card schema, manifest+signing, lifecycle, shared sandbox host crate, runtime-generic recognized set) is owned by the Universal Agent Runtime and published from the UAR repo. KnowMe retains the product layer: knowme:* capabilities (theme, app-shell chrome, Hands binding), marketplace, entitlement VC issuance, trust-pill/review UX, distribution channels, and the container-inversion roadmap. knowme_plugin_host remains the product host wrapping the UAR-owned shared host crate (D3 unchanged in structure).
  2. D1 target renamed: knowme:plugin@1.0.0 → uar:plugin@0.2.0 (version humility: 1.0.0 only after real plugins across ≥3 kinds and ≥2 hosts). The convergence now has four inputs, not three: knowme:plugin@0.1.0, librefang:plugin@0.1.0, uar-plugin.wit, and prometheus:component@0.1.0 (skill pack) — adjudicated in one UAR ADR (skill-task world).
  3. Host profiles introduced: headless (base host + skill-task + hook — librefang/BossFang nodes) and full-ui (+ events/a2ui/settings/app-shell/ provider — KnowMe). Cards declare profile_required; installers reject mechanically at install, not at runtime.
  4. Performance claims corrected (§2.2/D2): no "zero-cost"/"1–5 ms" blanket claims. Honest budgets: Cranelift ≈1.45–1.6× native on real workloads; iOS runs Pulley interpretation (~order of magnitude slower; .cwasm AOT native code cannot be loaded on iOS); JS components carry ~8 MB engine each; browser host is jco-transpiled (not wasmtime) with a host-parity conformance seam. Bundled-vs-synced distribution split for App Store 3.3.2.
  5. Settings substrate unified: JSON Schema 2020-12 everywhere (the draft-7 references in §2.9/§3.4 are superseded); one scope enum to be emitted from the Rust types (docs-from-code) — the README/plan scope-vocabulary divergence is a known defect.
  6. Twelve review holes have normative fixes (research doc Part 3 SR-1…SR-12): namespace proof (did:web/DNS-TXT or transparency log), signed advisory/ revocation blocklist with auto-quarantine, permission combination risk surfacing at install, host-stamped event provenance + emit-allowlist + rate caps, contributor reentrancy guard (no infer in pipeline stages), sidecar OS-fence + UDS broker, content-addressed generations with atomic payload+registry+catalog+settings swap and rollback, crash-loop circuit breaker, contribution ordering/aggregate budgets, universal action I/O schema validation, mobile execution reality (Pulley), and 0.2.0 versioning.
  7. app-shell / service / workflow worlds stay 0.x until proven; skill-task + hook ship first (evidence order).

S19-002 · Part 1 — Recommendation

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Part 1 — Recommendation

S19-003 · 1.1 The thesis

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

1.1 The thesis

KnowMe stops being "an app with features" and becomes a container whose only job is to provide the resources every AI application needs: identity, storage, settings, inference, memory, event transport (AG-UI), rendering contract (A2UI), tool interoperability (MCP), agent interoperability (A2A), policy (Cedar), and lifecycle supervision. Everything the user touches — chat, settings, memory, hands, every future feature — is a plugin against this container. Core features are simply first-party, pre-installed, pre-trusted plugins. The user must be unable to tell the difference.

This is the same inversion the industry has converged on: MCP standardizes agent→tool, A2A standardizes agent→agent, AG-UI standardizes agent→application event streams, and Google's A2UI (v0.9.1 current, v1.0 candidate) standardizes agent→rendered-UI. KnowMe's container requirement is exactly: understand AG-UI and A2UI, host WASM components, and get out of the way.

S19-004 · 1.2 Decisions (each with rationale)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Explicit amendments:
  • Key control does not establish reverse-DNS namespace ownership; separate registry proof is required.

1.2 Decisions (each with rationale)

D1 — One component model, one WIT family: uar:plugin@0.2.0 (amended 2026-08-04; was knowme:plugin@1.0.0 — see banner: UAR-owned, four-dialect convergence incl. prometheus:component). Today there are three divergent WIT dialects in the repo: knowme:plugin@0.1.0 (rust/crates/knowme_plugin_host/wit/knowme-plugin.wit), librefang:plugin@0.1.0 (rust/vendor/librefang/crates/librefang-skills/wit/), and uar-plugin.wit (vendored UAR). We converge them into a single knowme:plugin WIT package with multiple worlds (one per plugin kind: hook, service-contributor, agent, provider, app-shell). librefang's host interface set (fs, net SSRF-guarded, kv, agent, env, time) is the most mature and is adopted as the substrate of knowme:plugin/host; UAR's embedded-mobile profile becomes the mobile world variant. The builder-extensibility spec already flagged this convergence ("one extension component model… instead of two WIT dialects") — this plan executes it.

D2 — Wasmtime 46 everywhere; component model + WASI P2 only. knowme_plugin_host/Cargo.toml still references wasmtime 41 (commented out); both vendored hosts use wasmtime 46. Standardize on wasmtime 46, wasmtime::component::{Component, Linker, ResourceTable}, deny-by-default WasiCtx, and .cwasm precompiled caching (already in UAR's plugin_loader.rs). Rationale: component model gives language-agnostic plugins (Rust, TinyGo, Python via componentize-py, JS via ComponentizeJS/StarlingMonkey — the last already proven in librefang's wasmtime-wasi-http support), deny-by-default capability security, and 1–5 ms instantiation with precompiled cache. Core (non-component) modules are accepted only behind a compatibility shim for legacy skills.

D3 — Reuse librefang's sandbox_component.rs as the reference host; build knowme_plugin_host as the product host that wraps it. rust/vendor/librefang/crates/librefang-runtime/src/sandbox_component.rs is the most complete component host in the repo (capability subset wired at instantiation, undeclared imports → MissingCapability, typed host-error variants, additive-only semver policy). Do not write a third host. Extract/generalize that pattern into knowme_plugin_host behind a PluginHost trait so BossFang, UAR, and KnowMe mobile/desktop share one sandbox implementation.

D4 — Capability cards are the unit of advertisement; the manifest (.pxt, manifest v2) is the unit of distribution. Adopt the capability-card model from docs/strategies/plugins/README.md as-is: a plugin is a bundle that advertises capabilities (knowme:agent, knowme:tool, knowme:skill, knowme:hook, knowme:provider, knowme:ui-library, knowme:entity-schema, knowme:settings, knowme:theme) and is granted entitlements. Extend the recognized set v1.0 with three new capabilities required by the goals below: knowme:app-shell (full-application A2UI container), knowme:service (OpenAPI/HTTP service on an allocated port), and knowme:workflow (BossFang-orchestratable workflow).

D5 — AG-UI is the event bus; A2UI is the rendering contract; A2A/MCP are the interop surfaces. Terminology rule (already enforced in the strategy docs, restated because everything depends on it): - AG-UI (uar.agui/1 profile) — the event transport vocabulary. Every plugin that participates in a run emits/consumes AG-UI events through the existing, unit-tested seam gen_ui_protocol::{normalize_uar_agui_event, A2uiAdapter, AguiAdapter}. Plugins never invent their own event protocol. - A2UI (Google A2UI v0.9.1, uar.a2ui/1 profile) — the rendering contract. Every piece of UI a plugin shows — a settings form, a confirmation, a full application shell — is an A2UI surface rendered by the host's catalog (A2uiSurfaceView on Flutter, a2ui-{core,react,lit} on web/desktop). - MCP — tool exposure both directions (plugin tools appear in gen_ui_mcp's registry with McpServerTrust tiers; a plugin may itself mount an MCP server). - A2A — agent exposure (a plugin agent publishes an AgentCard and is reachable via the existing UAR A2A dispatcher/registry pattern).

D6 — Prompt-processing hooks are a typed pipeline, not scattered callbacks. Implement the hook pipeline already specified in docs/strategies/agents/README.md §3.1: ingress → intent-classify → route → context-assemble → prompt-build → [inference] → tool-gate → tool-execute → post-process → egress, as an explicit typed enum in gen_ui_agent. Rules carried from that doc, unchanged: declared not discovered (manifest announces stage + data classes), contribute don't mutate (typed, provenance-tagged, budget-capped contributions; 200 ms per-stage epoch budget; Cedar is sole authority at tool-gate). This is what makes the "context builder pattern" (scenario 1) work identically across system core, UAR core, and BossFang core.

D7 — Settings are a substrate, not per-plugin tables. Generalize UAR's existing SettingsManager.register_extension() (schema-as-data, JSON-Schema-validated writes) into a two-table settings_definition / settings_value substrate with scopes system | device | user | agent, exactly as specified in docs/strategies/plugins/README.md §11. Ownership levels: system core owns system scope, UAR core owns agent scope, BossFang core owns node scope; sensitivity secret ⇒ keychain/Vault reference, never inline value. A2UI settings forms are generated from schema + ui_hints, so a plugin's settings appear in the same Settings UI as core settings with zero per-plugin UI code.

D8 — Services get supervised sidecars with allocated ports, not in-process servers. A plugin that is "a web application or service exposing an OpenAPI spec on a unique port" runs as a supervised sidecar process (or WASM component with wasi:http), managed by a new ServiceBroker in knowme_plugin_host: port allocation from a per-instance range, health checks, lifecycle tied to plugin activation, OpenAPI spec ingestion at registration (operations become knowme:tool entries in the MCP registry, trust-tiered). Supply chain per the BossFang sidecar plan: cosign/SLSA/OCI verification before first spawn. The sidecar never gets a private API — all traffic from the container goes through the broker.

D9 — Plugins are first-class on mobile. No private APIs, no desktop-only features. The embedded UAR kernel (uar.a2ui/1, EmbeddedLibrary mode) and the Flutter A2uiSurfaceView renderer are already mobile-operational. WASM components run on mobile through the same wasmtime host (mobile world: reduced host imports, no wasi:http server sockets; sidecars disallowed on iOS, replaced by in-component service worlds). If a capability cannot be honored on a platform, the manifest says so and the UI degrades explicitly — the capability card carries a platforms field.

D10 — Distribution is content-addressed and signed. Keep knowme_plugin_host's existing model: WasmRef { cid, sha256 } (IPFS content addressing), ManifestSignature { publisher_did, signature_b64 } (Ed25519, did:key:), SignatureStatus { Verified, Unsigned, Invalid }, SandboxLimits (default 64 MiB / 30 s). Unsigned plugins install only into a developer trust tier with explicit user consent, mirroring gen_ui_mcp's McpServerTrust::{Untrusted, TrustedLocal} pattern.

S19-005 · 1.3 What this recommendation deliberately does NOT do

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

1.3 What this recommendation deliberately does NOT do

  • Does not invent a new event protocol (AG-UI profile exists and is tested).
  • Does not invent a new UI spec (A2UI is adopted, uar.a2ui/1 profile already in code).
  • Does not write a third WASM host (librefang's is generalized).
  • Does not give plugins direct network access (network flows through Cedar-gated host functions — net import with SSRF guard — or through uar-invoke("web-fetch", …)).
  • Does not allow plugins to render raw HTML/JS in the container (A2UI only; iframe embedding is available only inside an app-shell plugin's own surface and is catalog-mediated).

S19-008 · 2.2 Plugin kinds — how each required scenario maps

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.2 Plugin kinds — how each required scenario maps

All plugins share: manifest v2, capability cards, signed WASM component (or supervised sidecar), settings namespace, lifecycle. They differ in which WIT world they target and which capabilities they advertise.

# Scenario (from requirements) Plugin kind WIT world Advertised capabilities Execution model
1 System component: settings + network + reacts during prompt processing (system prompt, memory recall, RAG recall, skills activation) — the portable context builder Contributor knowme:plugin/contributor knowme:hook (stage list), knowme:settings, knowme:provider (optional) Host calls contribute(stage, context-in) → contribution at each declared pipeline stage; network only via net import (SSRF-guarded) or uar-invoke
2 Full application semantics: own A2UI component acts as an application shell container, composing other A2UI components/views across web/mobile/desktop App knowme:plugin/app-shell knowme:app-shell, knowme:ui-library, knowme:settings, optionally knowme:agent Registered as a navigation root; receives a root A2UI surface + catalog token; emits surfaceUpdate/dataModelUpdate; child surfaces resolve through catalog-first-then-contributed registry
3 Hooks only — called only on specific events Hook knowme:plugin/hook knowme:hook Event-subscription table in manifest (on: [run.started, tool.confirmation.requested, …]); invoked with epoch budget; no UI, no settings unless declared
4 Web app/service exposing OpenAPI on a unique port Service sidecar process or knowme:plugin/service (wasi:http component) knowme:service (openapi URL, port request), knowme:tool (generated) ServiceBroker allocates port, supervises process, ingests OpenAPI → MCP tools; health-checked; killed on deactivate
5 Image-inference provider (adds image support when the active model lacks it) Provider knowme:plugin/provider knowme:provider with modality: image-inference Registered in the inference router as a modality fallback; the local/UAR lane consults it when a request carries image input the primary engine rejects
6 Workflow referenceable by BossFang orchestration Workflow knowme:plugin/workflow knowme:workflow (graph ref) Declarative workflow document (nodes = capability invocations); executed by BossFang harness; progress streams as AG-UI events

A single .pxt bundle may combine kinds (e.g., an App that is also a Workflow and exposes an MCP server).

S19-009 · 2.3 The WIT family — `uar:plugin@0.2.0` *(amended 2026-08-04; authored in the UAR repo, consumed here)*

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.3 The WIT family — uar:plugin@0.2.0 (amended 2026-08-04; authored in the UAR repo, consumed here)

One package; host imports shared; worlds per kind. (Sketch — authoritative WIT lives in rust/crates/knowme_plugin_host/wit/.)

package uar:plugin@0.2.0;

// ---- shared host imports (capability subset granted at instantiation) ----
interface host-log     { log: func(level: level, msg: string); }
interface host-kv      { get: func(ns: string, key: string) -> option<list<u8>>;
                         set: func(ns: string, key: string, val: list<u8>) -> result<_, host-error>;
                         delete: func(ns: string, key: string) -> result<_, host-error>; }
interface host-settings{ get: func(key: string) -> option<json>;
                         set-own: func(key: string, val: json) -> result<_, host-error>; } // own namespace only
interface host-net     { fetch: func(req: http-request) -> result<http-response, host-error>; } // SSRF-guarded, Cedar-checked
interface host-events  { emit: func(evt: agui-event) -> result<_, host-error>;
                         subscribe: func(patterns: list<string>) -> result<subscription, host-error>; }
interface host-infer   { complete: func(req: inference-request) -> result<stream<inference-event>, host-error>; }
interface host-memory  { recall: func(query: string, k: u8) -> list<memory-hit>; } // Cedar-gated, provenance-tagged
interface host-a2ui    { push-surface: func(surface-id: string, msgs: list<a2ui-message>) -> result<_, host-error>; }
interface host-time / host-env / host-random  // as in librefang host.wit
interface host-error   { variant host-error { capability-denied(string), path-denied(string),
                         ssrf-denied(string), policy-denied(string), budget-exceeded, internal(string) } }

// ---- exports per world ----
world hook {
  include base-host;
  export handle-event: func(evt: agui-event) -> result<option<agui-event>, host-error>;
}
world contributor {
  include base-host;
  export contribute: func(stage: pipeline-stage, input: contribution-input)
                     -> result<contribution, host-error>; // typed, provenance-tagged, budget-capped
}
world agent {
  include base-host;
  export start-task: func(task: a2a-task) -> result<task-handle, host-error>;
  export poll-task / cancel-task;   // A2A-shaped, per agents doc §4.1
}
world provider {
  include base-host;
  export capabilities: func() -> provider-capabilities; // modalities, limits
  export infer: func(req: inference-request) -> result<stream<inference-event>, host-error>;
}
world app-shell {
  include base-host-with-a2ui;
  export init-shell: func(config: shell-config) -> result<_, host-error>;
  export on-action: func(action: a2ui-action) -> result<_, host-error>;
  export on-navigate / on-resume / on-suspend;
}
world service { // WASM-native service alternative to a sidecar
  include base-host;
  export handle: func(req: http-request) -> result<http-response, host-error>; // wasi:http aligned
}
world workflow {
  include base-host;
  export definition: func() -> workflow-document;
  export on-signal: func(signal: workflow-signal) -> result<_, host-error>;
}

Versioning policy (adopted from librefang): additive-only within a major version; undeclared imports fail at instantiation with MissingCapability; the host resolves compatibility ranges, not exact pins (per wasmCloud's VersionReq lesson).

S19-011 · 2.5 Lifecycle

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.5 Lifecycle

install → verify (signature → cid/sha256 → WIT world check → capability grant vs policy)
        → register (capability cards → registry; settings schema → substrate;
                    OpenAPI → broker ingest; A2UI catalog → registry merge)
        → activate (instantiate component w/ capability subset; allocate ports;
                    subscribe hooks; mount navigation)
        → deactivate (drain runs; kill sidecars; unsubscribe; keep data)
        → upgrade (verify new bundle; migrate settings values via schema versioning; atomic swap)
        → remove (deactivate + delete namespace data after user confirmation; audit record)

Every transition emits an AG-UI CUSTOM lifecycle event (knowme.plugin.*) and writes a Cedar-audited record.

S19-012 · 2.6 The hook pipeline (context-builder substrate)

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.6 The hook pipeline (context-builder substrate)

Implementation target: rust/crates/gen_ui_agent/src/pipeline.rs (new). Stages as a typed enum per agents doc §3.1:

pub enum PipelineStage {
    Ingress, IntentClassify, Route, ContextAssemble, PromptBuild,
    Inference, ToolGate, ToolExecute, PostProcess, Egress,
}
  • Contributors declare stages + data classes in the manifest; the pipeline never reflects over plugins to discover hooks.
  • contribute() returns Contribution { items: Vec<ContributionItem> } where each item is typed (SystemPromptFragment | MemoryHit | RagSlice | SkillRef | GuardrailRule), provenance-tagged (plugin-id, cid), and budget-capped (tokens + 200 ms epoch; over-budget ⇒ contribution dropped, telemetry emitted, pipeline continues).
  • The existing gen_ui_context factory (BudgetPlan, SliceKind, AssembleRequest) consumes contributions at ContextAssemble/PromptBuild; memory/RAG/skills activations become contribution inputs so a contributor can reshape recall across system core, UAR core, and BossFang core identically.
  • Cedar remains sole authority at ToolGate; hooks may propose guardrail rules, never grant.

S19-014 · 2.8 Service broker

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.8 Service broker

New module knowme_plugin_host::service_broker:

  • Port allocation: per-instance ephemeral range (default 43100–43199), leased on activate, released on deactivate; leases persisted so restarts are stable.
  • Supervision: sidecar process spawn/monitor/restart (max N restarts, backoff) reusing librefang's librefang-channels/src/sidecar.rs supervisor pattern and frozen sidecar protocol v1 (NDJSON-over-stdio) for control; WASM-native services instead run in the component host with wasi:http.
  • OpenAPI ingestion: at registration, fetch capabilities[knowme:service].openapi, validate (3.0/3.1), and generate knowme:tool entries into gen_ui_mcp's registry with McpServerTrust derived from the plugin's signature status; operations inherit the plugin's Cedar policy.
  • No private APIs: container↔service traffic goes through the broker's loopback proxy with per-plugin auth tokens injected by the broker; the service cannot be reached except through the broker.

S19-015 · 2.9 Settings substrate

Governing revision: PL-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.9 Settings substrate

Two tables, identical in SurrealDB (embedded) and Postgres (server), generalized from UAR's SettingsManager.register_extension():

settings_definition(slug, owner_plugin, scope: system|device|user|agent|node,
                    schema: jsonschema-draft7, ui_hints: json, sensitivity: plain|secret, version)
settings_value(slug, scope, scope_id, value | secret_ref, clock: crdt, updated_by, updated_at)
  • Writes validated against the JSON Schema; secret ⇒ keychain (mobile/desktop) or Vault ref (server).
  • Settings UI: host generates A2UI forms from schema + ui_hints and interleaves plugin sections into the existing Settings screen — plugin settings are indistinguishable from core settings.
  • A contributor/plugin reads its own namespace via host-settings.get; cross-namespace reads require an explicit permission and Cedar grant.

Case Behavior
Plugin panics/traps Run fails with structured error event; plugin marked degraded; 3 traps ⇒ auto-deactivate with notification
Over-budget hook Contribution dropped, telemetry, pipeline continues (never blocks the run)
Sidecar port conflict Broker retries next free port in range; range exhausted ⇒ activation fails with actionable error

App-shell emits unknown component Fail-closed error surface; incident logged with plugin id
Core/plugin API drift WIT compatibility ranges resolved at load; incompatible ⇒ plugin suspended with upgrade prompt

4.0 Execution model for the AI build agent

  • One phase = one openspec change (openspec/changes/<phase-name>/ with proposal/design/tasks), matching repo convention.
  • Task granularity: each task ≤ 1 focused PR; every task lists verification (test command + expected result) in tasks.md — the agent may not check a box without running the verification.
  • Conformance-first: before building features, build the conformance harness (P0) so every later phase has executable acceptance.
  • Dogfood gate: no phase is "done" until its capability is consumed by a first-party plugin, not only by test fixtures.
  • Hard constraints (from AGENTS.md/base rules): layering UI→Hooks→Stores→Services; Flat 2.0; entity state via prometheus-entity-management; all networking/LLM/persistence stays in Rust core; audit script must pass.
