Persistence expectations the UI relies on (owned by PEM/Rust, listed here because UI behavior depends on them): per-message entities with stable ordered block wrappers; stream checkpoints at semantic boundaries plus a short debounce; atomic finalization; crash restore reproducing exact block order, status, errors, settings, diagnostics, and branch identity.

S05-010 · 6. Chat thread — turn anatomy

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6. Chat thread — turn anatomy

S05-011 · 6.1 Ordered regions (formalized)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.1 Ordered regions (formalized)

An assistant turn renders, in order:

  1. Thinking region (0..n thinking blocks) — outside the answer bubble.
  2. Lifecycle region — the named-phase strip while the run is active; collapses to a summary line on completion (§6.4).
  3. Activity panels — toolUse/toolResult/skill/memory panels in stream order, outside the answer bubble.
  4. Answer bubble — text/code/artifact/image/divider runs, each maximal contiguous run wrapped in one surface, capped at 80% of viewport width (max 720 px), left-aligned.
  5. Citation attachments — adjacent to the answer content they support (§6.3).
  6. Terminal bubbles — persisted error or cancelled bubble after the last semantic block (§6.5).
  7. Action row — right-aligned, below the turn (§7.1).

The existing _AssistantTurn segmentation implements regions 1–5; this spec formalizes that behavior and adds the lifecycle strip and citation adjacency rules. Region backgrounds come from the surface ladder: panels on surface, the answer bubble on card/raised, thinking on the cyan-tinted surface (§6.2). No region may introduce a border, divider, or shadow.

S05-012 · 6.2 Thinking region

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.2 Thinking region

Behavior (formalizing ContentBlockThinking):

  • Expanded while streaming its own block; auto-collapses when answer content begins, unless the user manually expanded or collapsed it. A manual choice always wins over automation for that block.
  • Collapsed header shows: brain/psychology icon, "Thinking" label, and — once terminal — duration metadata ("Thought for 42 s"); while streaming, a live elapsed time replaces any spinner glyph.
  • Body is selectable plain text with whitespace preserved; no Markdown rendering inside thinking; copy button copies the raw trace.
  • Tint: cyan-tinted flat surface per design standard §7.5 (cyan = reasoning/citations/streaming). Current implementation uses the generic secondary surface — migrating to the cyan annotation tint is a formal delta of this spec, applied via tokens in both themes.
  • Android empty state: on the Android local lane (non-thinking Qwen), the region simply never appears. If a thinking toggle exists in settings (§13.3), it is shown disabled with the explanation "The on-device Android model does not produce reasoning traces."
  • Reasoning quarantine is invisible in day-to-day UX except one honesty touch: the inspector's prompt-plan view marks prior thinking blocks as excluded from context (§10.4).
  • Accessibility: header exposes expanded/collapsed state programmatically; body announces via polite live region while streaming; expanded thinking is reachable in keyboard focus order after the header.

S05-013 · 6.3 Citation attachments

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.3 Citation attachments

The Plan moves citations from "panel among panels" to adjacent to supported answer content:

  • citation blocks render as compact source chips inline at the end of the answer run they cite (trailing the bubble), not interleaved with tool panels. Each chip: source icon, short label, count badge when several chunks ground the same span.
  • Tapping a chip opens the citation card (existing _BlockSurface pattern): source title, excerpt, provenance (conversation / message / chunk / run), and — for memory citations — a "view memory" jump that opens the Memory destination at that record without losing thread position.
  • Fallback: when a citation arrives before its answer run exists (streaming edge), it renders in the activity-panel region and migrates adjacency on finalization. The block order on record never changes; this is a presentation rule only.
  • Citations use the cyan annotation tint; status is never by color alone (icon + "Citation · {source}" label).

S05-014 · 6.4 Lifecycle region (replaces `_RunStatusBubble`)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.4 Lifecycle region (replaces _RunStatusBubble)

While a run is active, a single strip above the answer area shows the run's named phase — this is the component the Plan requires to exist before any later stage may ship (no generic spinners downstream):

  • Content: phase icon + human phase label ("Retrieving memories", "Reading document", "Selecting tools", "Generating") + elapsed time + Stop affordance (44 px, accessible name "Stop generating").
  • Phase label mapping is a fixed table owned by the presentation layer; an unrecognized phase renders its snake_case name humanized — never a raw enum string, never blank.
  • The strip is a polite live region: it announces on phase change, not on every tick; elapsed time is visual only.
  • On completion the strip collapses to a one-line summary ("Generated in 8.2 s · on-device · CPU") which remains persisted with the message; on error/cancel it is superseded by the terminal bubble.
  • Queued/preparing states before the first phase event show "Preparing response" — this is a named state, not a spinner.
  • Model-bound phases (download, verification, loading, fallback selection) are normally surfaced by the model banner (§8.2); if a run hits them mid-thread (e.g. first send after install), the strip mirrors the same label so the user never sees a dead turn.

S05-015 · 6.5 Error and cancelled bubbles (extended)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.5 Error and cancelled bubbles (extended)

Existing _RunErrorBubble / _RunCancelledBubble are extended, not replaced:

  • Error bubble content, in order: error icon, safe message (plain language, from RunError.message — never a transport exception string), phase chip (e.g. "while loading model"), stable code in mono metadata, and a retry affordance when retryable ("Try again" re-runs the originating user message through the same path as Regenerate).
  • Non-retryable errors state the recovery path in one sentence ("This model file failed verification. Re-download it from the Models screen.") with a deep-link action where one exists.
  • Cancelled bubble: stop icon + "Response cancelled" + elapsed-before-cancel; no destructive styling (secondary surface).
  • Crash-restoration variant: when a restored message has a non-terminal run status that can never resume (process death), the terminal bubble reads "Interrupted when the app closed" with a "Regenerate" action. Restoration must reproduce exact block order, status, and diagnostics; partial blocks keep their content with a "restored partial response" metadata line.
  • Both bubbles persist with the message and appear in goldens (§15).

S05-016 · 6.6 Tool, skill, and memory panels (formalized)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.6 Tool, skill, and memory panels (formalized)

  • Panels render status, not raw JSON: pending → running → complete/failed with disclosure for input/output (existing _DisclosureBlock pattern).
  • AlwaysConfirm flow: a mutating tool renders the confirmation card in the panel region: tool name, human description of the mutation, parameters summary, consequence text, and Confirm / Deny actions (44 px, safe default = Deny, keyboard-focusable, announced as an alert). Confirmation resumes the exact stored call (existing local_tool_approve interaction); denial records a failed/skip result so the model can continue.
  • Restored confirmations that can no longer resume (process-local approvals) show the existing "resubmit to create a fresh approval request" guidance — keep this copy.
  • Repair attempts are visible: "Retrying tool call (2 of 2)" as panel status metadata, from the bounded-repair contract.
  • Skill panels show skill identity + status + output summary behind disclosure; memory panels distinguish recalled / proposed / written / updated / rejected (existing mapping) and link to the Memory destination.

S05-017 · 6.7 Backend chip

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.7 Backend chip

Every assistant turn carries a small metadata chip (mono, faint text, non-interactive-by-default): model short name + backend + lane, e.g. Qwen3-4B · CPU · on-device or Qwen3.5-9B · Metal · on-device or Gemma-4 · Cloud. When fallbackReason exists, the chip gains a warning icon and opens the inspector's diagnostics section on tap (e.g. "CPU selected: OpenCL requires a physical-device certification…"). Lane wording follows the standard's "On-device / My server / Cloud provider" trichotomy.

S05-018 · 7. Message actions and branch behavior

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7. Message actions and branch behavior

S05-019 · 7.1 Action inventory and rules

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.1 Action inventory and rules

Action On Behavior Disabled when
Copy block Every block header (exists) Copies that block's canonical text Never
Copy answer Assistant action row (exists) Copies answer-region blocks only (not thinking/panels) Empty answer
Copy message User bubble (exists) Copies full user content Never
Stop/Cancel Active run (send button morphs, exists; lifecycle strip, §6.4) Emits cancellation; terminal cancelled bubble follows Not disabled while active
Resubmit User message Creates a new branch: saved user content + attachments + branch prefix + current settings + newly assembled context plan Affected branch has an active run
Regenerate Assistant turn Branch-tail cleanup, then reruns the preceding saved user message Affected branch has an active run
Delete Assistant turn Confirms scope, removes response + branch tail, invalidates branch summaries, cleans solely-originating fact provenance Affected branch has an active run
  • The active-run disable rule is branch-scoped, not global: actions on other branches/conversations remain available. Disabled actions show a tooltip/explanation ("Wait for the current response to finish").
  • Delete confirmation copy states the blast radius: "Delete this response and the N messages after it on this branch? Memories saved from them are removed too." Confirm is destructive-styled; recovery is not promised.
  • All actions keep ≥48 px hit constraints (existing), tooltips, and accessible names; the action row is reachable after the turn content in focus order.

S05-020 · 7.2 Branch navigation (new)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.2 Branch navigation (new)

Branches are invisible today; the Plan makes them first-class:

  • Any message with siblings (created by Resubmit/Regenerate) shows a compact branch navigator trailing the turn: ‹ 2/3 › monochrome, 44 px targets, accessible label "Response 2 of 3, branch {branchId}".
  • Switching swaps the branch tail in place with the persisted block order of the selected sibling; scroll anchor stays on the navigator's message.
  • The active branch id is conversation state, restored on relaunch; the conversation header shows a "Branch" badge when viewing a non-main branch, with a "Jump to main" action.
  • The conversation library marks branched conversations (existing branched view expectation in the standard §7.8).
  • Branch creation is never silent: a one-line divider-less metadata row in the thread marks "Branched from an earlier message" at the fork point.

S05-021 · 8. Models surfaces

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8. Models surfaces

S05-022 · 8.1 Models screen (new — `features/models`)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.1 Models screen (new — features/models)

Design standard §9: "a user-owned library, not a storefront." Sections:

  1. Active model card — model name, quant (Q5_K_M), size on disk, lane ("On-device"), acceleration backend (CPU / OpenCL (Adreno) / Metal), device name, offloaded layers when known, and status (Ready, Not installed, operation-in-progress). Android copy names the model honestly: "Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, Q5_K_M, ~2.9 GB".
  2. Backend row — active backend with certification summary: "OpenCL locked: needs an on-device benchmark ≥15% faster than CPU" or "OpenCL certified: +23% median, thermally safe" or "CPU active: certification failed (correctness)". A "Re-run benchmark" action lives here (developer section mirrors it), producing the certification artifact the Rust gate consumes. Benchmark UX shows: running state with per-config progress (CPU run, OpenCL run), thermal readings, and the pass/fail verdict with the three criteria itemized.
  3. Available models — the pinned catalog (Android: Qwen3-4B; iOS: Qwen3.5 9B) with capability tags (text-only / vision / reasoning), context figures (§8.4), and per-model state + primary action (Download / Resume / Cancel / Delete / Activate).
  4. Remote models — BossFang-linked remote entries marked "Remote — runs on your server", visually and verbally distinct from local (standard §7.3 trichotomy); no remote row may look installed when it is not.
  5. Cloud presets — baked, versioned presets listed read-only with provider, model, and capability tags; enabling one requires the lane/BYOK configuration in Settings (§13.2) and is marked "Cloud".

Empty state (no model installed): explains local-first value, download size and time expectation, and one primary "Download Qwen3-4B" action — matching the standard's "one-action recovery" rule.

S05-023 · 8.2 Model operation banner (extended)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.2 Model operation banner (extended)

The existing chat _ModelOperationBanner extends to the full ModelOperationState machine:

  • States and copy: Not installed → slim info bar "No local model yet — chat uses cloud until one is installed" + action; Downloading → percent, data rate, resumable indicator ("resumes after interruption"), Cancel; Verifying → indeterminate-with-label; Loading → "Loading model into memory"; Ready → auto-dismiss with a transient confirmation; Cancelling → label only; Cancelled → "Download cancelled — resume anytime" + Resume; Failed → RunError safe message + retry/deep-link.
  • The banner is the single place model operations appear in chat; the Models screen shows the same state machine on the active-model card (one source of truth via the shared provider).
  • Polite live region announcing state transitions only; progress percent is visual.

S05-024 · 8.3 Download integrity presentation

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.3 Download integrity presentation

  • Verification state is named ("Verifying download"), never folded into the progress bar.
  • A failed checksum deletes the artifact and shows "Download failed integrity check and was removed" with a retry — this is the honesty standard applied to model files.
  • Byte counts use the pinned catalog values; resumed downloads show "resumed at N%" once.

S05-025 · 8.4 Capability honesty (nominal vs trusted context)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.4 Capability honesty (nominal vs trusted context)

Model rows and the inspector show two figures with an explainer (CTX §6.2): nominal context ("256K tokens — the model's advertised window") and trusted ceiling ("8K tokens — verified reliable on this device"). The explainer sheet (one tap on the figures) states: ceilings come from on-device measurements, 16K is available in Developer settings, and raising the ceiling trades reliability for history. iOS rows show the same pattern with the 9B profile.

S05-026 · 9. Composer and attachments

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

9. Composer and attachments

S05-027 · 9.1 Attachment strip (extended)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

9.1 Attachment strip (extended)

Existing chip strip (25 MiB / 6-file guards, error line) gains per-chip extraction state once sent is pressed and extraction begins:

  • pending → extracting → OCR → ready → failed, shown as a state dot + label on the chip ("Reading", "OCR", "Ready", "Couldn't read").
  • Android rule surfaced honestly: images and scans show "Text will be extracted — the on-device model can't see images directly" as a one-time hint under the strip (dismissible, per-conversation memory).
  • Extraction failure never blocks silently: the chip turns destructive-tinted with the safe message, and send proceeds only after the user removes the failed file or explicitly sends without it (a per-chip "Send anyway as file reference" is not offered on Android's text-only lane; cloud lane keeps original parts per the Xberg pipeline doc).
  • Limits remain: 25 MiB/file, 6 attachments, 512 KiB extracted text into context; hitting the text cap shows "Only the first part of this document fits the context" on the chip.

S05-028 · 9.2 Attachment blocks in the thread

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

9.2 Attachment blocks in the thread

Sent attachments render as artifact blocks (existing ContentBlockDocumentPreview path) with extraction metadata on disclosure: extracted length, OCR used (yes/no), and warning when extraction partially failed. The block header action copies the extracted text.

S05-029 · 9.3 Conversation documents panel (new)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

9.3 Conversation documents panel (new)

Plan §5: uploaded documents are conversation-scoped by default. A header-level "Documents" sheet per conversation lists:

  • Each ingested document: name, mime, size, chunk count, extraction state, and ingestion time.
  • Scope marker: "Stored with this conversation — deleted when it is deleted."
  • Promote to Knowledge action per document: moves chunks to durable knowledge with provenance intact; confirmation explains the scope change ("Available to all future conversations; governed by Memory settings").
  • Delete action per document (removes its chunks from this conversation's retrieval, with confirmation).
  • Empty state: "Files you send in this conversation can be searched in follow-up questions."

S05-031 · 10. Context inspector (new)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10. Context inspector (new)

One inspector surface unifies the Plan's context inspector and the design standard's activity/event inspector (§7.5) — a single progressive-depth sheet, not two debug models. Entry: telemetry chip on a turn, retrieval row, backend chip, or the model banner.

S05-032 · 10.1 Overview section

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.1 Overview section

Run identity (run id, message, branch), final status, timings per phase, backend/lane/diagnostics, model + profile name. This is the default landing section.

S05-033 · 10.2 Diagnostics section

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.2 Diagnostics section

RuntimeDiagnostics rendered readably: backend, device, offloaded layers, fallback reason (full text), thermal state during the run when recorded, and the certification reference when the backend is OpenCL.

S05-034 · 10.3 Context section (the Plan's inspector)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.3 Context section (the Plan's inspector)

From ContextTelemetryEvent + profile:

  • Profile row: baked capability profile name (device/model/runtime), estimator in use ("exact tokenizer" / "chars÷4 estimate"), and drift readout when comparison data exists ("estimate ran 12% hot this turn").
  • Envelope: trusted ceiling vs nominal context (§8.4), session envelope, output and safety reserves as fixed rows.
  • Slice spending: one row per slice — history, memory, knowledge, tools — with budget / spent / item count and a background-fill meter (Flat 2.0: a fill, not a bordered bar). The memory:knowledge split is labeled "30/70 fixed" and is not user-editable (§13.4).
  • Dropped items: list of dropped messages/chunks/tools with the reason (over budget, diversity dedup, recency decay, shortlist cap) — each row restorable for inspection ("what was dropped") but never re-injected from the UI.
  • Degradation badge: present when the run degraded (e.g. "Summarization unavailable → sliding window", "Thermal denial → reduced envelope"); badge text explains the visible consequence.
  • Thinking-cost hint: when thinking is enabled on a lane that supports it, the slice view shows the thinking reserve visibly reducing knowledge chunks (CTX §7.3), e.g. "Thinking reserve: 1,024 tokens (≈2 knowledge chunks)".

S05-035 · 10.4 Prompt plan view

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.4 Prompt plan view

A read-only, syntax-grouped rendering of the PromptPlan mirror: system, history window, memory/knowledge slices, tool schemas (shortlisted count shown: "4 of 11 tools offered"), and the exact exclusion markers — prior thinking shown struck-through-with-label "excluded from context". This is the sovereignty surface (CTX §11.2): the user can see precisely what will be sent. Copy action included; no editing here.

S05-036 · 10.5 Escalation card

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.5 Escalation card

When EscalationAdvice is present: a distinct card ("This device is struggling with this request") with the advice reason (thermal, envelope downgrade), the suggested action ("Continue on My server" / "Use a cloud preset"), and a one-tap handoff that resubmits the turn on the advised lane. No automatic lane switching ever happens without this explicit action.

S05-037 · 10.6 Events section

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.6 Events section

The standard's progressive-depth timeline: filter chips by family (lifecycle, content, context, tools, memory, telemetry), rows with sequence numbers, timestamps, and sanitized payload previews; unknown payloads render as the ArtifactBlock raw records they are. Replay action rebuilds the materialized thread from the append-only record without contacting the model. Payloads are sanitized — secrets and raw base64 blobs are elided.

S05-038 · 11. Conversation library (extended)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

11. Conversation library (extended)

The existing sheet gains the standard's required states:

  • Row metadata: title, relative time, message count, and state badges: running (phase label), failed (error icon + tint), branched (branch icon), local-only vs synced (privacy marker), per standard §7.8.
  • Running conversations keep running when the sheet or another conversation is opened; selecting a conversation cancels only view subscriptions.
  • Draft preservation: unsent composer text (and staged attachments) restore per conversation.
  • Search across titles and message text; recency groups Today / Previous 7 days / Older; row actions (rename, pin, archive, export, delete) in a context menu with destructive confirmation on delete ("Deletes this conversation, its branches, and its conversation-scoped documents. Promoted knowledge is kept.").

S05-039 · 12. Startup and lazy initialization (extended)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

12. Startup and lazy initialization (extended)

The Plan decouples startup: only FFI, the entity database, the SurrealDB schema, and compatibility metadata open eagerly; FastEmbed, seeds, Xberg/OCR, downloads, and inference initialize lazily with named status.

  • StartupGate keeps its current eager phase progress (migrations, schema) but the eager path must reach the usable shell within the 5-second cold- start gate; everything lazy moves out of the blocking sequence.
  • A lazy-init status surface replaces blocking spinners for deferred subsystems: a subtle header chip (or Home instrument row) listing deferred components with named states — "Document reader: starting" / "Embeddings: ready" / "Model: not installed". Each resolves independently; failures surface per-component with a retry, never as an app-level boot error.
  • Feature-level gating: invoking a feature whose dependency is still lazy (e.g. sending an attachment before Xberg is ready) shows the named preparation state inline ("Preparing document reader…") and completes without user intervention; it never dead-ends.
  • Boot errors remain blocking and visible only for the eager set (migrations/schema/FFI), per the existing _BootError.

S05-040 · 13. Settings and configuration schema

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

13. Settings and configuration schema

Settings becomes a real destination (features/settings). Every row: label, current value, and — where the value came from a layered override — a "source" hint (default / global / assistant / conversation). Tightening-only applies to all budget controls (§2.8).

S05-041 · 13.1 Appearance (existing)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

13.1 Appearance (existing)

Theme mode (system/light/dark). No change.

S05-043 · 13.3 Context & Memory

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

13.3 Context & Memory

  • History strategy: None / Sliding window / Truncate middle / Summarize / Hierarchical (CTX §8.1), with the per-strategy fields from CTX §4.2 (maxMessages; keepFirst 2 / keepLast 4 + omission marker; summarization model + 500-token cap + threshold 6; short-term 5 turns / mid 2,000 / long-term facts 500). Fields appear only for the active strategy.
  • Layered overrides: global default here; per-assistant override in the assistant's configuration; per-conversation override in the conversation's detail sheet. Each level edits only its own layer; effective value is shown computed with its source.
  • Truncate-middle transcript marker: when active, the thread renders the omission marker as a metadata row "[… 12 earlier messages omitted …]" (Divider-adjacent presentation: spacing + faint text, never a line).
  • Fact extraction (opt-in per assistant): an assistant list with a toggle per assistant, default off. Enrolling shows what it does ("Saves durable facts from this assistant's answers; visible in Memory; deletion respected"). A "Review extracted facts" link opens Memory filtered to facts with provenance (conversation / message / run), each deletable (CTX §8.5 sovereignty requirement).
  • Memory behavior: read-only summary of what enters future context (user content, assistant answers, tool outcomes, governed memory — never prior reasoning).

S05-044 · 13.4 Budget & performance

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

13.4 Budget & performance

  • Trusted ceiling: default 8K; the 16K extended ceiling is visible only with Developer mode on (decision inherited from CTX §15.5 — §17). The control only tightens below the profile ceiling (§2.8); copy explains the trade.
  • Memory/knowledge split: displayed as fixed "30 / 70" — not a user control (Plan fixes it).
  • Estimator: read-only current estimator + drift summary; comparison mode is a Developer tool (§13.6).
  • Thermal policy display: "Heavy work pauses when the device is hot" informational row, linked to escalation behavior (§10.5).

S05-045 · 13.5 Attachments & Documents

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

13.5 Attachments & Documents

  • Default scope explainer ("Files stay with their conversation unless you promote them"), promotion review link, and per-file/OCR limits listed (25 MiB, 6 files, 512 KiB extracted).

S05-046 · 13.6 Developer (behind a Developer-mode toggle)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

13.6 Developer (behind a Developer-mode toggle)

  • Extended 16K ceiling switch (§13.4).
  • Benchmark runner + last certification artifact viewer (correctness, thermal, median improvement, verdict) — the same data the Models screen summarizes.
  • Estimator comparison readouts; telemetry ring viewer (bounded local ring, newest-first).
  • Protocol/event console: the inspector's Events section without a run context.
  • Copy of build pins: Flutter 3.45.0-0.1.pre, Dart 3.13.0, Rust 1.96, FRB 2.12, Android arm64 / API 29.

S05-048 · 14. Accessibility and motion requirements (per surface)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

14. Accessibility and motion requirements (per surface)

Global floor: WCAG 2.2 AA as itemized in §2.10. Per-surface specifics:

  • Streaming text/thinking: polite liveRegion semantics; no per-token announcements — announce phase changes and completion, not deltas.
  • Thinking/panels: expanded state programmatic (Semantics(expanded:)); disclosure controls labeled; focus order: panels → answer → actions.
  • Lifecycle strip: phase transitions announced; Stop reachable by keyboard at all times during a run; Escape cancels when focus is in the thread.
  • Confirmations (tool/delete/promote): alert semantics, safe default focused first, destructive action last in order, Escape = safe choice.
  • Branch navigator: Semantics(button, label: 'Response 2 of 3'); switch announced.
  • Charts/meters in the inspector: meter fills are decorative; values always paired with text (never color-only), slices readable top-to-bottom by screen reader.
  • Targets: 44×44 for all touch actions (existing 48 px constraints meet this); inspector chips ≥44 px.
  • Text scaling: all layouts verified at 130% and 200% scaler without overflow; bubbles use max-width + flexible wrapping; the inspector tables collapse to stacked rows at ≥130%.
  • Reduced motion: auto-scroll becomes instant (exists); strip transitions, panel expansions, and sheet presentations become opacity-only or instant; no parallax or physics animations anywhere in these surfaces.
  • Themes: every surface specified here renders in both palettes from KnowMeTheme; cyan/ember/status tints verified against resolved foreground pairs, not token names.

S05-049 · 15. Golden and behavior test matrix

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

15. Golden and behavior test matrix

Per flutter-golden-ui: real KnowMeTheme wrapper, deterministic pumps (fonts loaded, animations off, fixed sizes, settled), one golden per meaningful state × light/dark, goldens/<widget>_<light|dark>.png. Alchemist is the configured harness.

Sizes: 320 px and 768 px widths; text scale: 1.0 and 2.0 on selected rows; states as listed per widget.

Widget/surface Golden states (×2 themes)
Thinking region streaming-expanded, auto-collapsed, manual-expanded, terminal-with-duration
Lifecycle strip each representative phase (retrieval, OCR, tool selection, generation), stopped-cancelled
Error bubble retryable with phase chip, non-retryable with deep-link, crash-restored
Cancelled bubble standard, restored-partial
Tool confirmation card pending confirm, confirmed-running, failed, restored-unresumable
Citation chip + card single, multi-source, memory-citation
Answer bubble markdown+code, mermaid, narrow-320 at 2.0× text
Action row full, disabled-during-active-run
Branch navigator 1/2, 2/3, with fork metadata row
Model banner download 40% resumable, verifying, loading, failed-checksum, cancelled-resume
Models screen empty, installed-CPU, installed-OpenCL-certified, benchmark-running, remote-marked
Documents panel empty, scoped list, promoted item, extraction-failed
Inspector overview, slices with drops+degradation, prompt plan with exclusions, escalation card
Conversation library badges (running/failed/branched), groups, search results
Startup eager phases, boot error, lazy-status chip states
Settings sections each section both themes; developer section

Behavior tests (widget-level, 3–5 per feature at the public surface): thinking auto-collapse on answer start (and manual-override precedence); active-run disabling of Resubmit/Delete/Regenerate; branch navigator switching swaps tails; banner cancel → cancelled state; confirmation approve/deny interaction payloads; attachment chip failure removes-or-blocks send; extraction-state transitions; tightening-only budget control rejects increases; live-region announcements fire on phase change only.

S05-051 · 17. Open questions (decisions required before implementation)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

17. Open questions (decisions required before implementation)

  1. Destination count (§4.2): fold Models into Settings (recommended) or accept a 6-destination deviation.
  2. 16K extended context in v1 UI (inherited CTX §15.5): this spec assumes Developer-flag-only; confirm.
  3. Fact-extraction default (inherited CTX §15.2): this spec assumes per-assistant opt-in, off by default; confirm against a global opt-in.
  4. Citation adjacency migration (§6.3): confirm the presentation-only re-flow (panel → adjacent chip at finalization) versus keeping citations in the panel region permanently.
  5. Mermaid renderer: current flutter_mermaid (WebView-class) is kept; pure-Dart rendering remains unviable upstream. Confirm continued WebView dependency with the existing source/accessible fallback.
  6. Benchmark runner placement: Models screen action (this spec) vs Developer-only; exposing it to all users makes the OpenCL gate self-serve but invites thermal test abuse. Leaning: keep in Models with a cooldown + explanation.

S06 · knowme-ui-ux-standard.md · 48 sections

Open complete source record · Technical text

S06-001 · KnowMe UI/UX Standard

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Explicit amendments:
  • Mobile presentation is native Flutter; shared Rust semantics remain. See RT-01–11.

KnowMe UI/UX Standard

Status: Binding product-design standard Applies to: React 19 web/PWA, Tauri desktop, Flutter iOS/Android, generated KnowMe surfaces, and shared UI packages Last updated: 2026-07-17

S06-002 · 1. Purpose and authority

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

1. Purpose and authority

KnowMe should feel like a private, capable personal-intelligence workspace: calm enough for sustained thinking, transparent enough to trust, and powerful without looking like an infrastructure console.

This standard consolidates the intended experience from the KnowMe functional specification, implementation plan, mood board, user journeys, and current product direction. When an older mockup conflicts with this document, this document wins. In particular, the older mood-board mockups use borders, divider lines, and shadows that are now explicitly superseded by the Flat 2.0 rules below.

The standard is specific enough to serve as:

  • an implementation contract for React and Flutter;
  • an acceptance checklist for design and code review;
  • the source for scaffold and design-token rules;
  • a reference for future OpenDesign artifacts; and
  • the basis for visual-regression, accessibility, and cross-platform parity tests.

S06-003 · 2. Product experience

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2. Product experience

S06-004 · 2.1 Product promise

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.1 Product promise

KnowMe is “AI that understands you.” It combines private memory, local and user-controlled inference, agent workflows, and cross-device continuity. The interface must make three facts obvious:

  1. The system is ready and the user can act immediately.
  2. The user can see which model and device are doing the work.
  3. The user remains in control of what is stored, synchronized, or sent elsewhere.

S06-005 · 2.2 Primary users

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.2 Primary users

The mood board identifies four overlapping audiences:

  • knowledge workers who need rapid synthesis and continuity;
  • privacy-conscious professionals handling sensitive material;
  • builders and developers who want inspectable system behavior; and
  • cross-device power users who expect conversations and memory to follow them across devices they control.

The UI therefore needs consumer-grade clarity with professional information density. It must not become either a sparse marketing page or a developer-only dashboard.

S06-006 · 2.3 Experience qualities

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.3 Experience qualities

Every KnowMe surface should be:

  • Personal: use human language, remembered context, and a stable sense of place.
  • Local-first: clearly identify on-device, user-owned remote, and commercial cloud execution.
  • Inspectable: expose model, tool, citation, memory, and agent activity without flooding the default view.
  • Calm: use restrained color, few simultaneous calls to action, and predictable motion.
  • Fast: acknowledge input immediately and stream meaningful output as it arrives.
  • Honest: show real readiness, progress, provenance, and errors; never fake completion.
  • Continuous: preserve drafts, history, scroll position, selected model, and conversation state.

S06-007 · 3. Flat 2.0 is non-negotiable

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3. Flat 2.0 is non-negotiable

KnowMe uses a strict Flat 2.0 visual language.

S06-008 · 3.1 The rule

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.1 The rule

Do not use lines or borders anywhere. Differentiate adjacent screen areas and components only with background-color changes. Spacing, typography, shape, and content establish hierarchy within those areas; they are not substitutes for a required surface-color change.

This applies to application shells, titlebars, sidebars, tab bars, cards, inputs, buttons, menus, dialogs, chat bubbles, code blocks, tables, tool calls, citations, thinking panels, media, and Flutter equivalents.

S06-009 · 3.2 Required treatment

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.2 Required treatment

Need Flat 2.0 treatment
Separate page from navigation Use adjacent canvas and navigation background tokens.
Separate sections Use spacing or alternating surface tokens.
Group content Use a filled surface with modest radius and internal spacing.
Show hover Shift to the hover background token.
Show selection Use an accent-tinted background plus stronger text/icon color.
Show keyboard focus Use a high-contrast focus background plus a visible icon, label, or state cue so focus does not depend on color alone.
Show input affordance Use a distinct filled field background, placeholder, and cursor.
Show table structure Use row background changes, alignment, and whitespace—not grid lines.
Render a protocol divider Use vertical space or a surface transition, never an <hr> line.
Show elevation/modal priority Dim the underlying canvas and use a distinct modal surface; avoid drop shadows.

S06-010 · 3.3 Prohibited treatment

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.3 Prohibited treatment

  • No border, border-*, outline used as decoration, separators, or input chrome.
  • No one-pixel rules between sidebars, headers, rows, messages, or composer regions.
  • No card outlines, even transparent outlines that become visible on hover.
  • No bevels, skeuomorphic highlights, glassmorphism, gradients, or glossy controls.
  • No layout-defining drop shadows. A modal scrim is the preferred depth cue.
  • No default Material Divider, OutlineInputBorder, or outlined button variants.
  • No Shadcn defaults may be accepted without removing their border-based styling.
  • No status should be communicated by color alone.

S06-011 · 3.4 Flat does not mean blank

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.4 Flat does not mean blank

Use a deliberate four-level surface ladder so hierarchy remains immediately legible:

  1. Canvas — the page background.
  2. Chrome — titlebar, sidebar, bottom navigation, and persistent utility areas.
  3. Surface — major panels, composer, menus, and grouped content.
  4. Raised surface — selected, expanded, modal, or actively streaming regions.

Large undifferentiated empty areas are not acceptable. Empty states must explain the value of the screen and offer a relevant first action.

S06-012 · 4. KnowMe visual identity

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4. KnowMe visual identity

S06-013 · 4.1 Color system

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.1 Color system

Color is restrained. Most of the interface is monochrome surface differentiation. Ember is the brand/action color; cyan represents AI annotation and remote/streaming intelligence; green, amber, and red are reserved for status.

Role Dark Light Use
Canvas #0B0F14 #F7F7F8 Primary application background
Chrome #111620 #FFFFFF Navigation and persistent chrome
Surface #161D29 #FAFBFC Panels and grouped regions
Raised surface #1C2535 #FFFFFF Selected/expanded/modal regions
Hover surface #202B40 #F2F4F7 Pointer and keyboard interaction
Muted surface #253044 #EEF0F3 Inputs, secondary controls, skeletons
Primary text #E8EDF3 #0B0F14 Titles and body text
Secondary text #A7B0BC #4B5563 Supporting information
Faint text #6B7280 #6B7280 Metadata that still passes contrast
Ember #FF6A3D #E04E28 Brand, primary action, active destination
Cyan #00C2DC #0891B2 Reasoning, citations, streaming, user-owned remote AI
Success #22C55E #16A34A Ready, connected, completed
Warning #F59E0B #D97706 Degraded or attention needed
Error #EF4444 #DC2626 Failed or destructive state

Legacy border tokens should resolve to transparent or be removed. They must never create visible geometry.

S06-014 · 4.2 Typography

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.2 Typography

  • Space Grotesk: display headings and concise screen titles; tight tracking.
  • Inter: navigation, controls, labels, and normal application copy.
  • Roboto: optional long-form reading and assistant prose where it improves readability.
  • JetBrains Mono: code, model identifiers, timestamps, measurements, event labels, and compact metadata—not entire screens.

Use responsive type roles rather than arbitrary sizes. Body copy should normally be 15–17 logical pixels with a comfortable line height. Do not shrink core UI copy below 12 logical pixels. Respect OS/browser text scaling without clipping or fixed-height text containers.

S06-015 · 4.3 Logo and iconography

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.3 Logo and iconography

  • Use the rounded-bar K monogram with the ember node at its joint.
  • The wordmark is Know plus ember Me.
  • Keep the logo optically clear against a single flat background.
  • Use one coherent line-icon family, normally Lucide on React and its closest semantic Flutter equivalent.
  • Icons support labels; they do not replace labels for unfamiliar or consequential actions.

S06-016 · 4.4 Shape, spacing, and motion

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.4 Shape, spacing, and motion

  • Use modest, consistent radii. Controls are softly rounded, not excessively pill-shaped.
  • Reserve pills for compact status, model/lane identity, and metadata.
  • Use a 4-pixel spacing base with an intentional rhythm: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, and 48.
  • Motion should explain state change. Use short opacity/background transitions and restrained expansion.
  • Honor prefers-reduced-motion and Flutter accessibility settings.
  • Never animate merely to make an idle screen feel busy.

S06-017 · 5. Responsive application shell

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5. Responsive application shell

S06-018 · 5.1 Desktop and wide web

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5.1 Desktop and wide web

  • Use a branded custom titlebar in Tauri with platform-correct window controls.
  • Use a left navigation rail/sidebar for top-level destinations.
  • Keep the main work area centered within sensible reading widths while allowing data views to expand.
  • The active destination uses an ember-tinted background and label/icon emphasis, not an outline.
  • Persistent system status—active model, local/remote lane, sync, and readiness—must be available without opening settings.

S06-019 · 5.2 Phone and narrow web

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5.2 Phone and narrow web

  • Replace the rail with a bottom navigation bar based on width, not OS sniffing.
  • Keep the primary action/composer above safe areas and the on-screen keyboard.
  • Use a two-column capability grid only when labels remain readable; otherwise use one column.
  • Never squeeze the desktop sidebar into a narrow rail of unexplained icons.

S06-020 · 5.3 Tablet

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5.3 Tablet

  • Prefer an adaptive rail plus flexible content.
  • Conversation history may become a collapsible pane; it must not permanently consume the reading area.

S06-021 · 6. Component and state standard

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6. Component and state standard

S06-022 · 6.1 React 19 component stack

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.1 React 19 component stack

Use these layers deliberately:

  • Shadcn UI is the default component vocabulary for buttons, inputs, menus, dialogs, sheets, sidebars, tabs, tooltips, scroll areas, command palettes, and accessible primitives.
  • Assistant UI owns the chat thread primitives, composer behavior, message lifecycle, thread list integration, streaming affordances, actions, attachments, and assistant-specific interaction model.
  • @prometheus-ags/gen-ui-react owns exhaustive rendering of the shared ContentBlock protocol.
  • React 19 components implement KnowMe-specific compositions and rich renderers.
  • Raw HTML controls should not be introduced when a suitable Shadcn primitive exists. Semantic HTML remains required underneath those components.

Shadcn and Assistant UI are starting points, not permission to ship their default appearance. Every component must use the KnowMe tokens and Flat 2.0 treatment. Remove visible borders, separator rules, default shadows, and unrelated neutral palettes.

S06-023 · 6.2 Client state and persistence

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.2 Client state and persistence

TanStack Query is not part of the KnowMe architecture.

  • Prometheus Entity Management 3.x is the entity/query/mutation/reactivity layer for conversations, messages, blocks, citations, attachments, and related client entities.
  • Zustand stores ephemeral interaction state: active thread ID, composer draft, selected blocks, open panels, temporary stream assembly, scroll intent, and presentation preferences.
  • PGlite persists browser/PWA conversation entities in IndexedDB-backed storage, preferably through a shared worker for safe multi-tab ownership.
  • pglite-oxide persists the same relational conversation model in the Tauri Rust layer. React reaches it through typed Tauri commands/events; it does not open the desktop database directly.
  • SQLite + sqlite-vec is the mobile relational/vector equivalent behind Rust repository traits because pglite-oxide does not support iOS or Android.
  • SurrealDB remains the graph-memory/RAG store. Conversation citations may reference memory entities without duplicating the graph as component state.

React visual components follow this chain:

Component → feature hook → Zustand/Prometheus Entity Management → platform transport → database or Rust command

Flutter follows:

Widget → @riverpod provider → repository/service → Rust FFI → platform database

S06-024 · 6.3 Required ownership boundaries

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.3 Required ownership boundaries

These libraries are complementary and must not be treated as interchangeable choices:

Concern Required owner
General React controls, navigation, overlays, and sidebars Shadcn UI, restyled with KnowMe tokens
Thread, composer, attachments, message actions, streaming lifecycle, and thread list Assistant UI
Normalized durable entities, queries, mutations, and reactive projections @prometheus-ags/prometheus-entity-management 3.x
Active selection, panel visibility, draft interaction, scroll intent, and in-progress stream assembly Zustand
Browser/PWA relational persistence ElectricSQL PGlite in IndexedDB
Tauri desktop relational persistence pglite-oxide owned by Rust and exposed through typed commands/events
Mobile relational persistence SQLite/sqlite-vec behind the same Rust repository contracts
Personal memory graph and local RAG retrieval SurrealDB plus the shared Rust memory/RAG pipeline
Cross-surface message and agent output The shared AG-UI/ContentBlock protocol

Installing Shadcn UI or Assistant UI without mounting their primitives at the real interaction boundary does not satisfy this standard. Likewise, keeping conversations in an in-memory Zustand array, while PGlite is merely present as a dependency, does not satisfy persistence. Durable records must be written incrementally and restored after a real page refresh or application relaunch.

S06-025 · 7. World-class conversation experience

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7. World-class conversation experience

S06-026 · 7.1 Conversation layout

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.1 Conversation layout

The chat screen consists of four coordinated regions:

  1. Conversation library — multiple conversations, search, new conversation, rename, pin, archive, delete, and optional grouping.
  2. Conversation header — title, model/lane identity, readiness, sync/provenance, and contextual actions.
  3. Thread viewport — virtualized messages and rich streamed blocks with stable scroll behavior.
  4. Composer — multiline input, attachments, voice entry where supported, model/lane access, stop/regenerate, and send.

On wide screens the library is a Shadcn sidebar. On narrow screens it is a Shadcn sheet/drawer opened from the header. Assistant UI thread-list and thread primitives should be adapted to these surfaces rather than recreating chat behavior by hand.

S06-027 · 7.2 Multiple conversations

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.2 Multiple conversations

Users must be able to:

  • create a conversation instantly and type before persistence finishes;
  • return to any prior conversation with its model, messages, citations, and artifacts intact;
  • search titles and message content;
  • see useful recency groups such as Today, Previous 7 Days, and Older;
  • rename, pin, archive, export, and delete conversations;
  • preserve unsent drafts per conversation;
  • continue the same synchronized conversation on another owned device;
  • branch from a message or regenerate without silently destroying the earlier answer; and
  • understand whether a conversation is local-only, synced to owned infrastructure, or includes cloud calls.

The empty state should offer focused starter actions based on KnowMe capabilities, not a blank transcript.

S06-028 · 7.3 Default local-first behavior

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.3 Default local-first behavior

Chat must work out of the box without asking the user for provider credentials.

  • Tauri defaults to an available local model and can download the product-default model with explicit progress.
  • Browser/PWA defaults to WebLLM when WebGPU is available, with model caching in browser storage.
  • If a local model is unavailable, explain what is needed and offer a one-action recovery; never expose a raw bridge exception as assistant content.
  • Cloud providers are optional enhancements configured later.
  • “On-device,” “My server,” and “Cloud provider” must be visually and verbally distinct.

S06-029 · 7.4 Streaming behavior

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.4 Streaming behavior

  • Echo the user message immediately.
  • Create one assistant message and incrementally update its blocks; do not append one message per token.
  • Preserve the event ordering emitted by the Rust protocol pipeline.
  • Keep auto-scroll attached only while the user remains near the bottom. If the user scrolls upward, show a “jump to latest” action rather than stealing position.
  • Provide stop generation, retry, copy, branch, and feedback actions.
  • Show a subtle streaming state in the active content region; do not rely on a generic spinner when tokens or structured events are available.
  • Persist events incrementally so a crash does not erase a long response.

S06-030 · 7.5 AG-UI/A2UI event presentation

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.5 AG-UI/A2UI event presentation

The protocol event stream is product-visible evidence, not debug noise. Store the append-only event record and project it into an exhaustive ContentBlock view.

Block/event Required presentation
Text Streaming Markdown with stable typography and copy support
Thinking Collapsed by default; cyan-tinted flat surface; duration/token metadata; user-controlled expansion
Code Language label, copy action, optional filename, syntax highlighting, and safe wrapping/scrolling
Citation Inline citation markers plus expandable source cards with title, source, excerpt, and jump/open action
Memory Explain whether memory was read, proposed, written, updated, or rejected; allow inspection and user control
Tool use Named step with pending/running/completed/failed state and inspectable input
Tool result Structured result paired with its tool call; errors are explicit and recoverable
Skill Skill identity, status, parameters, and useful output summary
Artifact Dedicated preview for code, document, visualization, or generated component; preserve source/download
Image Accessible alt text, constrained preview, open/download action, and provenance
Divider Spacing or surface transition only—never a visible line
AG-UI state delta Update the relevant visible state without dumping raw JSON into the thread
Confirmation request Accessible Shadcn dialog/surface with consequences, choices, and safe default; resume the agent after response

New protocol variants must cause compile-time exhaustiveness failures until React and Flutter renderers are implemented.

The user may open an activity/event inspector for a run. It presents the same ordered event stream at progressively deeper levels rather than inventing a second debug-only model:

  • the normal thread shows human-readable text, thinking, memory, citation, tool, skill, confirmation, state, and artifact blocks;
  • an expanded block shows its timing, status, model/lane, provenance, and related event span;
  • an advanced timeline can filter by event family and reveal sanitized payloads, sequence numbers, run IDs, retries, and parent/child relationships; and
  • replay uses the persisted append-only events to rebuild the materialized thread without contacting the model again.

Memory/RAG citations are first-class relationships. A citation chunk links the answer span to the retrieved memory or source chunk, shows relevance and provenance, and lets the user inspect the underlying memory without losing their place in the conversation. Thinking chunks remain collapsed by default, stream live when expanded, and clearly distinguish model reasoning summaries from tool activity or factual sources.

S06-031 · 7.6 Markdown and rich media

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.6 Markdown and rich media

Assistant prose supports CommonMark plus carefully selected extensions:

  • GitHub-flavored tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks, footnotes, and fenced code;
  • syntax-highlighted code with copy and accessible language metadata;
  • Mermaid diagrams rendered lazily in a contained React component, with source and accessible text fallbacks;
  • sanitized SVG preview—never execute arbitrary script, event handlers, or external references from model output;
  • images with alt text, dimensions, provenance, and safe loading behavior;
  • audio/video players with controls, captions/transcripts when available, poster/fallback states, and no autoplay;
  • downloadable artifacts with explicit type and size;
  • optional math rendering when a product workflow requires it.

Rich content must not use unsafe raw HTML. Sanitize Markdown extensions and remote media, enforce URL/content policies, and give users a source-view fallback when a renderer fails.

Implement each rich format as a typed React 19 renderer registered with the Assistant UI thread, not as string replacement inside one monolithic message component. Renderers must be lazy where their dependency is expensive, preserve stable keys while streaming, expose an error boundary and source fallback, and avoid blocking ordinary text rendering. Mermaid, SVG, images, video, audio, and artifacts open in a Shadcn sheet/dialog or an optional side-by-side artifact workspace while the conversation remains visible.

S06-032 · 7.7 Chat visual treatment

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.7 Chat visual treatment

  • Assistant responses should read as authored content within the canvas, not as an endless stack of outlined bubbles.
  • User messages may use an ember-tinted filled surface aligned to the trailing edge.
  • Thinking, citations, tools, and artifacts use distinct background tokens and labels while remaining borderless.
  • Keep readable prose width even when the overall workspace is wide.
  • Keep the composer visually anchored with a distinct filled surface; do not draw a box around it.
  • Errors use a dedicated error surface with plain-language recovery, never raw invoke/JavaScript/Rust errors in the transcript.

S06-033 · 7.8 Conversation library and workspace behavior

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.8 Conversation library and workspace behavior

The conversation library is part of the working product, not decorative sidebar chrome. It must be backed by the same persisted conversation entities as the thread and support:

  • a prominent new-conversation action and immediate optimistic selection;
  • full-text search across titles and message text;
  • pinned, recent, archived, local-only, synchronized, and branched views;
  • contextual rename, pin, archive, export, and recoverable-delete actions;
  • unread/running/failed state without requiring the user to open each thread;
  • per-conversation model, execution lane, draft, attachments, and last-read position; and
  • responsive presentation as a persistent desktop sidebar or Shadcn sheet on narrow layouts.

Selecting another conversation must cancel only view subscriptions; it must not cancel an unrelated background run. Running conversations continue to persist events and expose their status in the library. Returning to one restores its thread, active artifacts, expansion state, draft, and scroll anchor.

S06-034 · 8. Data model for durable chat

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8. Data model for durable chat

The web and desktop schemas should be logically equivalent even when their platform adapters differ.

erDiagram
    CONVERSATION ||--o{ MESSAGE : contains
    MESSAGE ||--o{ CONTENT_BLOCK : projects
    CONVERSATION ||--o{ AGUI_EVENT : records
    MESSAGE ||--o{ CITATION : cites
    MESSAGE ||--o{ ATTACHMENT : includes
    CONVERSATION ||--o{ DRAFT : preserves
    CONVERSATION o|--o{ CONVERSATION : branches_from

Minimum durable records:

  • conversations: identity, title, timestamps, lane/model preference, sync/privacy mode, parent/branch metadata, pinned/archived state;
  • messages: conversation, role, ordering, status, timestamps, generation metadata;
  • content_blocks: ordered typed payloads and stable IDs;
  • agui_events: append-only event ID, run ID, sequence, event type, payload, timestamp;
  • citations: message/block relationship, memory/source identity, excerpt, location, provenance;
  • attachments: metadata, content address, local/cache location, MIME type, dimensions/duration;
  • drafts: per-conversation composer content and attachment references.

Persist raw protocol events for replay/audit and maintain materialized entities for fast UI rendering. Event IDs and sequence numbers make retries idempotent. Database migrations are versioned and shared at the repository-contract level.

flowchart LR
    UI["Shadcn + Assistant UI"] --> Hooks["Feature hooks"]
    Hooks --> Zustand["Zustand ephemeral state"]
    Hooks --> PEM["Prometheus Entity Management 3.x"]
    PEM --> Web["Web transport"]
    PEM --> Desktop["Tauri transport"]
    Web --> PGlite["PGlite + IndexedDB"]
    Desktop --> Rust["Rust commands + event channels"]
    Rust --> Oxide["pglite-oxide"]
    Rust --> Agent["LLM / AG-UI pipeline"]
    Agent --> Desktop
    Agent --> Blocks["ContentBlock projection"]
    Blocks --> UI

Settings and sync

Models

S06-042 · 10. Flutter parity

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10. Flutter parity

React and Flutter must express the same semantic design system, not merely similar colors.

  • Generate both CSS variables and Flutter ThemeData/ThemeExtension values from one versioned token source.
  • Match semantic surface, text, status, spacing, radius, typography, and motion roles.
  • Use shadcn_flutter components where they provide the matching accessible interaction; otherwise build token-driven Flutter components with the same semantics.
  • Do not use stock ThemeData.dark(), ColorScheme.fromSeed, outlined fields, Divider, or default Material elevation as substitutes for the KnowMe theme.
  • Use width-based bottom navigation versus rail behavior consistently with React.
  • Render the same ContentBlock union exhaustively and preserve AG-UI confirmation/state behavior through Riverpod and Rust FFI.
  • Pixel identity between browser and Skia is not required; semantic token and interaction parity is.

S06-043 · 11. Accessibility and trust

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

11. Accessibility and trust

  • Meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast for text, controls, focus, and status.
  • Support keyboard-only navigation, logical focus order, skip navigation, and screen-reader landmarks.
  • Every icon-only control requires an accessible name and tooltip where appropriate.
  • Streaming updates use polite live regions and must not repeatedly interrupt screen readers.
  • Expanded/collapsed reasoning, tool, and citation sections expose state programmatically.
  • Respect reduced motion, high contrast, text scaling, and platform safe areas.
  • Destructive actions explain scope and require confirmation when recovery is not immediate.
  • Privacy/execution labels use text and iconography in addition to color.

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Visual

  • No visible borders, divider lines, or layout shadows remain.
  • Adjacent regions are distinguishable through approved background tokens.
  • Light and dark modes both use the KnowMe palette and pass contrast checks.
  • The ember accent remains restrained; cyan and status colors retain their meanings.
  • Empty, loading, streaming, degraded, offline, and error states are intentionally designed.

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Components and architecture

  • React uses Shadcn UI for general primitives and Assistant UI for chat/thread behavior.
  • Flutter uses the corresponding token-driven/shadcn_flutter patterns.
  • Prometheus Entity Management 3.x—not TanStack Query—owns entity reactivity and mutations.
  • Zustand contains transient UI state, not the durable conversation database.
  • Web conversations persist in PGlite; desktop conversations persist through Rust in pglite-oxide.
  • Visual components call hooks rather than stores, database clients, or Tauri invoke() directly.

S06-047 · Chat

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Chat

  • A new user can send a prompt using a local model without provider configuration.
  • Multiple conversations can be created, searched, resumed, renamed, and archived.

Responsive and cross-platform

  • Review at 320, 768, 1024, and 1440 CSS pixels in both themes.

S07-007 · 4.2 cherry-studio fork (`src/renderer/.../contextStrategy.ts` + agent lane)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.2 cherry-studio fork (src/renderer/.../contextStrategy.ts + agent lane)

The fork defines exactly four managed strategies plus none, a layered resolution model, and telemetry. Honest implementation status, verified in source:

Strategy Config Chat apply path Persistence
sliding_window maxMessages (else dynamic by token budget) Fully wired — takeLastMessages —
truncate_middle keepFirstMessages=2, keepLastMessages=4, showOmissionMarker Fully wired — first+last slices —
summarize summarizationModelId, summaryMaxTokens=500, summarizeThreshold=6 Falls back to sliding window in the synchronous path TopicContextMetadata.conversationSummary, summarizedMessageIds
hierarchical shortTermTurns=5, midTermSummaryTokens=2000, longTermFactsTokens=500 Falls back likewise TopicContextMetadata.longTermFacts, factsUpdatedAt

Additional fork mechanics ported into the fabric:

  • Layered resolution: resolveEffectiveChatContextStrategy merges global → assistant → topic overrides key-by-key; agents default to { type: 'none' } and opt in separately. Ported as StrategyResolver (§8.1).
  • Agent pre-compact: shouldRunSdkCompactBeforeTurn compares the prior turn's total-token usage (usage cache) against compactTriggerTokens and runs a compaction step before the next user message. Ported as the PreCompactPolicy on cloud/agent sessions (§8.6).
  • Telemetry: ContextManagementStreamPayload (tokensBefore/After/Saved, messagesRemoved, alterationSummary, trigger). Ported as ContextTelemetryEvent on the AG-UI stream (§12).
  • Hygiene filters: the fork runs a fixed filter chain (context-clear, useful-message, error-pair, adjacent-user, user-role-start) before the strategy. The fabric keeps the same two-phase shape: normalize → strategize.
  • Token estimation: the fork uses chars/4. Acceptable for Electron; not acceptable as the only estimator on-device (§6.5).

The port obligation: all four strategies become real in Rust — the fork's fallback behavior for summarize/hierarchical is a TypeScript-renderer limitation, not a design decision to preserve.

S08-014 · 5.3 UI: two render targets, one event bus

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5.3 UI: two render targets, one event bus

  • HTMX/server-rendered fragments — the extension component exports render(surface, props-json) → html and the container injects the fragment into a sandboxed webview/iframe with the plugin-bridge (window.knowme.invoke/subscribe — the deferred v0.2 surface in FUNC-SPEC §08; this spec is the concrete driver for it). The htmx-alpine-lit skill in the skill pack is the authoring guide; forge's htmx-alpine-animations-research.md already explores the idiom.
  • A2UI components over AG-UI — for the Flutter tier and rich React surfaces the extension emits AG-UI events (the POC's gen_ui protocol crates and the KnowMe UI/UX standard already speak AG-UI); the container's gen_ui renderer materializes A2UI component trees. Extension UI is therefore data, not code, on this path — which is what makes the same extension render on web, desktop, and mobile.

Both paths ride one bus: extension → emit-event → container event router → (HTMX swap | AG-UI stream). Agent-generated UI and extension UI are the same mechanism.

S18-005 · 4. A2UI — the one UI plane

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4. A2UI — the one UI plane

Plugins never ship React or Flutter code. UI is A2UI components as data: declared in the capability card, rendered by the shared renderers — Flutter via the official GenUI SDK (gen_ui_widgets' A2uiSurfaceView, Google A2UI v0.9), React via UAR's a2ui-* packages — over the UAR production profile uar.a2ui/1 (Google A2UI v0.9.1, catalog urn:uar:a2ui:catalog:1). The transport underneath is the AG-UI event stream (docs/strategies/ag-ui/README.md); AG-UI is the event vocabulary, A2UI the validated rendering contract — the two are never the same channel. Component definition, registry, storage, selection, and renderer conformance are specified in docs/strategies/a2ui/README.md, which governs wherever this section sketches. Wiring is declarative: a component binds to the capability's actions (user gesture → A2A task) and events (task status → component state), so interactivity round-trips through the same audited bus as everything else. A2UI is the normalization story: one component library per plugin, identical on every platform. Chunk type a2ui-patch is how streaming operations update live components mid-generation.

S19-013 · 2.7 A2UI app-shell model

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.7 A2UI app-shell model

  • An app-shell plugin receives a root surface and the host catalog token (urn:uar:a2ui:catalog:1 base + its own contributed catalog, resolved catalog-first-then-contributed, fail-closed — per the A2UI strategy doc).
  • The host shell mounts it as a navigation peer of Chat/Settings/Memory; the plugin composes views by emitting surfaceUpdate / dataModelUpdate / beginRendering messages (A2UI v0.9.1; adopt v1.0's actionResponse RPC when finalized).
  • User interactions return as typed A2uiActions (already implemented end-to-end: A2uiSurfaceView → Riverpod → Repository → FFI on Flutter; a2ui-react on web/desktop).
  • Core features migrate to the same model (Part 4, P4) — this is what makes "user cannot tell core from plugin" true rather than aspirational.
  • A2UI registries may be served by plugins (flint-forge already exposes an A2UI registry as MCP at /mcp/v1/a2ui — the pattern to generalize).

  • P3.2 Catalog merge + fail-closed rendering; contributed-catalog persistence (SurrealDB a2ui_schema per A2UI strategy doc).
