S22-001 · A2UI Strategy — Component Registry, Definition, Storage, and Selection

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

A2UI Strategy — Component Registry, Definition, Storage, and Selection

Scope: A2UI as KnowMe's single declarative UI plane — the component catalog (vocabulary governance), where component/surface definitions live (definition), how they persist and roam (storage), how a run picks and renders one (selection), and the renderer conformance gate. This is the completion plan for the "A2UI registry and component definition/storage/selection" gap.

Status: v1.1 strategy, 2026-07-19 (v1.1 aligns ownership with the integration doc: UAR owns the catalog; KnowMe owns rendering conformance). Grounded in the vendored UAR submodule (rust/vendor/universal-agent-runtime v1.0.0, src/uar/a2ui/) and the existing Flutter renderer (flutter_packages/gen_ui_widgets). The governing ownership split is docs/strategies/uar-knowme-runtime-integration.md ("A2UI catalog integration"). Companions: docs/strategies/ag-ui/README.md (the event transport that carries A2UI traffic), docs/strategies/plugins/README.md §4 (knowme:ui-library capability cards), docs/strategies/agents/README.md (agent UI surfaces), PAGS-SPEC-KM-UIX-001 (turn-level rendering).

S22-002 · 1. Terminology and the standing rule

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

1. Terminology and the standing rule

AG-UI is the event transport vocabulary; A2UI is the validated declarative rendering contract (UAR README). The standing security rule, from both UAR and the plugins doc: A2UI artifacts map to an approved component catalog and never execute model-provided or plugin-provided HTML/JavaScript. The component vocabulary is the sandbox.

S22-003 · 2. What exists today (verified 2026-07-19)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2. What exists today (verified 2026-07-19)

S22-004 · In UAR (`src/uar/a2ui/`)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

In UAR (src/uar/a2ui/)

  • protocol.rs — the validated production profile: uar.a2ui/1 over Google A2UI v0.9.1, catalog id urn:uar:a2ui:catalog:1. Serde DTOs with deny_unknown_fields: A2uiMessage (Create / Components / Data / Delete) and a Component enum (Text, Button, TextField, CheckBox, ChoicePicker, …) — the enum is the approved catalog, enforced at deserialization.
  • schema.rs — ArtifactSchema: the definition of one A2UI surface type.
  • registry.rs — A2uiRegistry: resolves a2ui_schema_id → schema. In-memory only.
  • routes.rs — REST: schema listing + user-response ingestion.
  • Runtime flow: an agent declares UI surfaces in its UAR-AGENT-MD (§06); the runtime emits agui.artifact_input_request SSE events; the frontend renders form/confirm/select widgets; the user's response re-enters the paused run as a tool result.
  • Reference renderers (React): uar/frontend/packages/a2ui-core (vendored Google @a2ui/web_core, version-pinned v0.8/v0.9), a2ui-react, -lit, -svelte, -inspector, -uar.

S22-005 · In KnowMe

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

In KnowMe

  • Flutter renderer exists: gen_ui_widgets' A2uiSurfaceView renders Google A2UI v0.9 JSONL through Flutter's official GenUI SDK (package:genui) — protocol state machine, surface lifecycle, schema validation, reactive data binding included — and emits a typed A2uiAction (surfaceId, name, sourceComponentId, timestamp, context, optional clientDataModel). It is wired into the thread as the artifact block kinds a2ui / application/a2ui+json, with actions forwarded through Riverpod → Repository → FFI (layering intact).
  • No KnowMe-side registry, storage, or selection logic yet — the renderer consumes whatever a block hands it; nothing owns the catalog, validates a surface against a registered schema, or records which components exist.

S22-006 · 3. The four open problems

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3. The four open problems

S22-007 · 3.1 Definition — one catalog of record, three producers

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.1 Definition — one catalog of record, three producers

Components and surfaces come from three producers: the UAR catalog (first-party vocabulary, UAR-owned, base = urn:uar:a2ui:catalog:1 at the pinned submodule version), agent artifacts (UAR-AGENT-MD §06 surface declarations), and plugin ui-library cards (plugins doc §4). One schema format governs all three: the UAR ArtifactSchema shape, extended with a namespaced id (knowme:a2ui:* first-party; reverse-DNS for plugins, same rule as capability ids) and a semver version. Authoring new first-party components means extending the catalog URN with a version bump — vocabulary governance per plugins doc §4.2.1, never ad-hoc per-producer shapes.

S22-008 · 3.2 Storage — UAR owns the catalog; KnowMe persists a cache plus contributions

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.2 Storage — UAR owns the catalog; KnowMe persists a cache plus contributions

The ownership line (integration doc): UAR owns the catalog registry and the supported component profiles; KnowMe owns rendering conformance. Storage falls into two classes accordingly:

Class Contents Store Lifecycle
Catalog cache The approved UAR catalog profiles (urn:uar:a2ui:catalog:1 at the pinned submodule version, plus later UAR-issued updates) Reproducible from the pinned artifact at boot; optionally persisted as an offline-rendering cache on mobile (the integration doc's "cache approved profiles for offline rendering") Refreshed only with a submodule/catalog update; version surfaced in diagnostics
Contributed schemas Plugin ui-library components, installed agent surfaces SurrealDB a2ui_schema records: {id, version, schema_json, source (plugin/agent id), content_hash, installed_at} Persist across restart; sync with the plugin/agent definition they arrived with (definitions travel, grants don't — plugins doc §10); removed on uninstall

KnowMe's registry module (behind FFI, not a Flutter construct) resolves a2ui_schema_id across both classes, catalog first, then contributed, with exact-version then compatible-minor semantics. It is a conformance cache and contribution store, never a competing catalog authority: components whose ids are not in the UAR catalog or an installed contribution are rejected (fail closed, §3.3). The embedded UAR instance keeps its own in-memory registry for its own surfaces; the two are synchronized at agent/plugin install time, never merged ad hoc.

S22-009 · 3.3 Selection — deterministic resolve-then-negotiate

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.3 Selection — deterministic resolve-then-negotiate

When a run wants to show a surface:

  1. Declare — the agent artifact or skill carries a2ui_schema_id + minimum vocabulary version (UAR-AGENT-MD §06 / capability card ui).
  2. Resolve — the registry returns the schema (§3.2) or a typed schema_not_found (which renders as an honest fallback panel, never a crash).
  3. Negotiate — the renderer on this platform checks the schema's component set against its supported vocabulary: full support → render; partial → render supported components + labeled fallback for the rest (plugins doc §4.2.1: "a labeled fallback, never a crash or a blank"); below minimum vocabulary → labeled fallback with an upgrade hint. Fail closed on the unknown: a component id outside the UAR catalog and all installed contributions is never executed or rendered as an interactive element — the labeled fallback is the closed failure surface, and the rejection is logged with the run's provenance (integration doc: "unknown catalog ids or component names fail closed").
  4. Interact — user gestures produce typed A2uiActions (Flutter: the existing A2uiSurfaceView callback) routed Riverpod → Repository → FFI → the paused run as its tool result (UAR's routes.rs ingestion in server placements; KnowMe's service-mode facade now calls the same /api/uar/runs/{run_id}/artifact-response seam; embedded mobile remains the future in-process equivalent). Local interaction stays local: inputs echo and validate on-device; the bus sees semantic events ("form submitted"), never keystrokes (plugins doc §4.2.3).

S22-010 · 3.4 Conformance — parity is a gate, not an intention

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.4 Conformance — parity is a gate, not an intention

Per plugins doc §4.2.2: one schema source generates both platforms' types; a conformance suite of golden renderings runs on both renderers per catalog version. Concretely: fixture surfaces exercising every catalog component × light/dark × phone/wide, golden-tested in Flutter (flutter-golden-ui harness, Alchemist) and screenshot-tested in React; divergence is a bug with an owner. The Flutter renderer's GenUI SDK pins Google A2UI v0.9 — track the UAR profile's v0.9.1 patchline deliberately; a profile bump is a reviewed submodule + catalog update, not a background drift.

S22-011 · 4. Settings surfaces are the first consumer

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4. Settings surfaces are the first consumer

The generic settings engine (plugins doc §11) generates A2UI forms from settings_definition.schema + ui_hints — every plugin, agent, and provider gets a settings page on every platform for free, rendered through exactly this registry/selection path. That makes settings the proving ground for §3 before agent-authored surfaces arrive: same schema format, same negotiation, same fallback rules, zero bespoke settings UI.

S22-012 · 5. Completion plan (releases)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5. Completion plan (releases)

  • A2UI-R1 — Registry + storage. a2ui_schema SurrealDB table; KnowMe registry module behind FFI with the two-class resolution; catalog cache load at boot; schema_not_found fallback panel (both renderers).
  • A2UI-R2 — Selection + negotiation. Vocabulary-version capability check per platform; labeled partial/fallback rendering; A2uiAction → run-resume wired through the UAR service facade and routes.rs for server placements, with embedded mobile as the remaining in-process lane.
  • A2UI-R3 — Settings-form generator. schema + ui_hints → A2UI form surfaces for plugin/agent/provider settings (consumes R1+R2).
  • A2UI-R4 — Conformance gate. Shared fixture set; Flutter goldens + React screenshots per catalog version in CI; divergence blocking.
  • A2UI-R5 — Agent/plugin surfaces. ui-library card installation into the contributed store; UAR-AGENT-MD §06 surfaces flowing through embedded UAR; agui.artifact_input_request end-to-end on mobile (rides the agent-skills roadmap's Release C certification).

S22-013 · 6. Invariants (do not regress)

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6. Invariants (do not regress)

  • No model- or plugin-provided HTML/JS ever executes; unknown components degrade to labeled fallbacks.
  • A2UI traffic rides the AG-UI stream and the ContentBlock projection (artifact blocks) — no parallel UI channel.
  • Renderers inherit design tokens and Flat 2.0 from the host theme; plugins cannot go off-brand by construction (plugins doc §4.1).
  • The component vocabulary is versioned registry data; renderer parity per version is tested, not aspirational.
  • Actions crossing the bus are semantic, typed, and audited like any tool result — including the confirmation surfaces for mutating tools (UIX-001 §6.6), which are A2UI forms with AlwaysConfirm policy, not a special case.

S29-010 · AG-UI/A2UI execution ownership

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

AG-UI/A2UI execution ownership

UAR owns the complete live artifact loop, not only the component registry. For every A2UI-producing turn UAR must:

  • create and persist the source run;
  • emit the official AG-UI run, step, text, reasoning, tool, state, artifact, error, cancellation, and completion events;
  • validate and publish A2UI surface messages and state patches;
  • retain surface replay data for reconnect/restart recovery;
  • accept typed A2UI actions against the durable source run;
  • merge the submitted client data model and action context under UAR policy;
  • create and stream the continuation run through the same AG-UI protocol; and
  • own component-library promotion, versioning, and governance.

React and Flutter are deliberately thin clients in this loop. They render the approved catalog, maintain only transient form state, persist the projected conversation blocks, and send a typed action envelope containing sourceRunId, surfaceId, sourceComponentId, action name/context, timestamp, and the client data model. They do not synthesize continuation prompts, execute agent logic, or guess which UAR run owns a restored surface.

The acceptance gate is an actual prompt → UAR run → A2UI surface → client restart/reload → restored surface → typed action → UAR continuation → AG-UI completion sequence. A display-only fixture or client-local callback does not qualify.

S29-011 · A2UI catalog integration

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

A2UI catalog integration

UAR owns the catalog registry and supported component profiles. KnowMe owns rendering conformance:

  • Flutter must implement the approved UAR/A2UI catalog components needed by the mobile experience.
  • Unknown catalog ids or component names fail closed.
  • Component registry updates come from UAR, but mobile can cache approved profiles for offline rendering.
  • A component action always targets the persisted UAR source run; an ephemeral client run map may be used only as a same-session fallback.
  • Renderer tests should use UAR golden fixtures where available, not hand-authored one-off examples only.

S29-016 · Phase 3 — Real skills and A2UI registry

Governing revision: UI-01–11 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Phase 3 — Real skills and A2UI registry

  • Register a real UAR skill fixture in mobile.
  • Certify visible SkillBlock lifecycle from UAR, not only MCP namespace derivation.
  • Render a UAR-managed A2UI surface from the approved catalog.
  • Persist and restore the UAR skill/A2UI blocks from entity-records.sqlite3.
  • Keep UAR skill activation chunks first-class: selectable/copyable, ordered in the turn timeline, persisted separately from answer Markdown, and excluded from future prompt context by default unless UAR policy opts in.

10Context, models, memory and knowledge

CX-01 — One context fabric. gen_ui_context resolves device, model and runtime profiles plus measured session envelope into an effective budget. The builder owns ordering, truncation, tool shortlisting, retrieval and escalation. UI adapters load profiles and display decisions; they do not duplicate budget arithmetic. A model's advertised context length is not its measured reliable retrieval capacity.

CX-02 — Budget invariant. System, tool schemas, history, memories, knowledge, output reserve, reasoning reserve and margin must fit the effective ceiling. Exact tokenizer counts are preferred; heuristic estimates carry an explicit wider margin and telemetry. Context presets in the retained source are initial targets. Validate their arithmetic on every turn, especially when reasoning is enabled, rather than assuming source tables are internally additive. Thermal pressure or sustained latency reduces the local budget and offers an explicit handoff choice.

CX-03 — Strategies. Preserve sliding window, truncate-middle with counted omission marker, progressive summary, hierarchical short/mid/long-term memory, and pre-compact triggers. Never split a tool call from its result. Summaries store covered turn IDs and provenance. If summarization fails or is thermally disallowed, fall back visibly to sliding window for that turn. Fact extraction is opt-in and writes through the governed memory store rather than a hidden second memory.

CX-04 — Retrieval. Preserve atomic short notes, semantic boundary chunking, recursive overlap, and parent-child retrieval. Chunks have stable document/ordinal IDs, source spans, token estimates and ingestion provenance; document replacement is transactional. Separate memory and knowledge budgets prevent a large document from starving explicit personal memory. Fuse eligible vector/BM25/graph lanes, apply bounded diversity/recency ranking and deterministic placement. A cross-encoder is a measured follow-up, not a default mobile burden.

CX-05 — Model resolution. Global role slots, agent/Hand pins, deployment-target configuration and conversation overrides resolve to a permitted provider/model with required capabilities. Preserve provider::model identity, embedding model/dimension stamps, re-embedding migrations, explicit cloud consent and local-only usage-based suggestions. Remote fallback is a proposal, never a silent privacy downgrade. A model unavailable on the current device produces an honest state with alternative placement choices.

CX-06 — Acquisition. Retain curated catalog provenance, license gating, user-chosen model imports, resumable downloads, content integrity, available storage checks, hardware/memory probes, and post-download validation. Source engine/model combinations are lane-specific and historically dated. Certify model load, tokenizer/template correctness, bounded generation, tool/structured output semantics and physical-device resource behavior against actual artifacts. A successful download is not a successful local inference deployment.

CX-07 — Knowledge base. Preserve source-linked knowledge/wikis, incremental ingestion, link/provenance graphs, stale-source detection, index rebuilds and export. Derived summaries do not overwrite originals or acquire higher authority than their sources. Deletion propagates through eligible indexes and derived artifacts with an inspectable receipt; it cannot recall previously disclosed text from another participant or provider.

CX-08 — Capture and tools. Ask Image, Audio Scribe, Prompt Lab and Skills remain first-class workflows. Vision/OCR/document extraction preserve attachments and source spans; Audio Scribe keeps recording, transcription, speaker labels and summaries distinct; Prompt Lab supports ephemeral single-turn templates and model comparison; Skills distinguish atomic tools from packaged practices with instructions and policy proposals. MCP is an adapter at the edge, not a bypass around grants or budgets.

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Local Inference Engine
On-device LLM inference using candle with GGUF quantized models downloaded from HuggingFace Hub. Metal-accelerated on Apple Silicon; rayon BLAS multi-core on Android. The inference loop runs entirely on the Tokio blocking thread pool — never touching the SSE event loop.

S07-002 · 1. Executive summary

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

1. Executive summary

KnowMe's promise — "it knows the user" — is delivered through three inputs (memories, dropped-note RAG, tools) fed to models whose real capacity varies by two orders of magnitude across deployment targets: a Q4_K_M Qwen3.5-4B on a Galaxy S25 Ultra is not a cloud frontier model, and pretending otherwise produces an app that works in demos and fails in pockets. Today, context assembly is implicit and scattered: gen_ui_agent::chat builds message lists ad hoc, gen_ui_db_graph retrieves without budget awareness, tool schemas are injected wholesale, and nothing enforces the token arithmetic that on-device models require.

This specification defines one context fabric: a gen_ui_context crate in the shared Rust core that owns (a) a three-layer capabilities model (device / model / runtime) resolved into an EffectiveBudgetPlan, (b) a deterministic ContextBuilder pipeline that fills that plan in a fixed order, (c) the four context-management strategies from the Cherry Studio fork, ported natively (sliding window, truncate-middle, progressive summarization, hierarchical memory) plus the agent pre-compact trigger, (d) a chunking subsystem for dropped documents, and (e) a retrieval/re-ranking pipeline (existing RRF → MMR diversity → recency decay → placement policy). Every surface — Flutter mobile, Tauri desktop, web/WASM, Axum cloud — consumes the same crate through the same trait seams already used for InferenceProvider; platforms differ only in the capability profile they load, never in pipeline logic.

The design thesis is the same as the rest of the Fabric: architectural correctness over feature count. The model plans nothing about its own context; the harness owns budgets, ordering, truncation, and escalation as deterministic Rust. This is not a stylistic preference — the research base (§3) shows small on-device models measurably cannot self-manage tool memory, long contexts, or multi-step state, and that structured subsystems recover most of the gap.

S07-003 · 2. Scope, goals, non-goals

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2. Scope, goals, non-goals

Goals

  1. A single capability + budget abstraction controlling: system prompt size, history window, memory injection count/tokens, knowledge-base retrieval count/tokens, tool shortlist size, tool-schema tokens, output reserve, thinking reserve, re-ranking configuration — on every platform.
  2. Port the four fork strategies as first-class Rust implementations with the fork's layered override model (global → assistant/agent → topic/session).
  3. Chunking for dropped notes/documents with provenance, integrated with the existing gen_ui_db_graph ingest path without breaking atomic short notes.
  4. Deterministic, testable assembly: same inputs + same profile ⇒ same prompt, byte-for-byte, on every platform.
  5. Telemetry parity with the fork (tokensBefore/After/Saved, alteration summary) surfaced on the AG-UI stream.

Non-goals (v1)

  • Cross-encoder re-ranking (deferred behind a measurement gate, §10.4).
  • Model fine-tuning / LoRA for tool calling (separate initiative; §3.4 notes when it becomes the higher-leverage move).
  • Changing the embedding model or EMBED_DIM (stays 384 / all-MiniLM-L6-v2).
  • Prompt-content authoring (skills/personas). This spec governs assembly and budgets, not what the system prompt says.

S07-004 · 3. Research foundation (condensed, with sources)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3. Research foundation (condensed, with sources)

Findings gathered across this design session; each shaped a specific mechanism below. Full citations in §16.

3.1 Effective context ≪ nominal context. Qwen3.5-4B and -9B share an identical 32-layer hybrid layout — 8 × (3 × Gated DeltaNet → 1 × Gated Attention), full_attention_interval: 4 — so both have exactly 8 full-attention "precision checkpoints"; the difference is width (2560 vs 4096 hidden), not checkpoint density. GDN layers compress history into fixed-size recurrent state; precise recall depends on the 8 full-attention layers. Nominal 262K is a training capability, not a usable retrieval window. Consequence: 8K operating ceiling, 16K only behind an explicit degraded-mode flag; reliable RAG budget is low thousands of tokens (§7 tables).

3.2 Quantization compounds with context length. 8-bit ≈ −0.8% on long-context suites; 4-bit methods lose up to 59% worst-case, damage growing past 8K; K-quants are gentler than GPTQ/BNB-nf4 but Q4_K_M is still 4-bit. The GDN-recurrent-state × 4-bit interaction is uncharacterized in the literature — an explicit empirical risk. Consequence: needle-in-haystack smoke test against our actual GGUFs is a Phase 0 gate, not an afterthought.

3.3 Position matters ("lost in the middle"). Small models retrieve worst at 20–70% depth. Consequence: the placement policy (§10.3): best hit last (adjacent to the query), second-best first, middle treated as distractor space.

3.4 Agentic limits. Success ∝ (1−p)^m — 99% per-step accuracy is 36.6% at 100 steps; per-step accuracy itself degrades with step count (self-conditioning). Deviations on mutating actions reduce success odds by up to 92–96%; read-only deviations barely matter (SABER). Tool-selection accuracy degrades past ~20–25 exposed tools; Anthropic measured 58 tools ≈ 55K tokens. Two-stage retrieve-then-load gives ~6× system-prompt reduction and 10–25× context-growth reduction (TinyAgent/ToolRAG lineage). Small models cannot self-manage tool memory (MemTool); structured subsystems close the gap (fastWorkflow). Consequence: max 3–4 autonomous steps before checkpoint, individual gates on all mutating actions, 5–8 tool shortlist ceiling, harness owns planning. A purpose-LoRA over our real schemas becomes the better investment only after a tool cluster stabilizes — not before.

3.5 Thermal envelope is a budget dimension. Sustained inference: iPhone −41.5% throughput plateau (Hot state by ~iteration 17); S25-class GPU cliffs 680→231 MHz at 78.3 °C; shell >42 °C in 100 s at peak; dense on-device RAG prefill has exceeded 14 s TTFT in published deployments. Consequence: the SessionEnvelope (§6.4) tracks cumulative inference and degrades or hands off to cloud; RAG budgets also bound prefill latency, not just recall.

3.6 Structured output. Grammar-constrained decoding (llguidance, already a declared-but-unwired feature of our vendored llama-cpp-2) makes malformed JSON structurally impossible; it fixes shape, not semantics. Consequence: wire llama-cpp-2/llguidance into both mobile composite features; keep in-prompt tool descriptions to name + one line; compile grammars once per session; temp 0.0–0.2 on structured turns; post-parse semantic validation; 1–2 capped repair retries then fail closed.

4. Current-state review

S07-006 · 4.1 know-me-system (Rust workspace)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.1 know-me-system (Rust workspace)

What exists and is kept:

  • InferenceProvider trait seam (gen_ui_inference): engines behind a trait; Android = LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 E2B through the Rust boundary, iOS retains the existing llama.cpp/Qwen lane until re-certification, desktop has its own local engine lanes. The context fabric slots in as a sibling seam, not inside any engine.
  • Hybrid retrieval (gen_ui_db_graph): SurrealDB search::rrf fuses vector + BM25 lanes; rrf.rs fuses the RELATE graph-hop lane (k=60, limit=20) with an explicitly documented constraint — RRF only for lanes that can agree; disjoint-ordered lanes score by hop distance. Kept as-is; the new pipeline wraps it (§10).
  • Embedder trait (embed.rs): 384-dim, model-provenance check, batch API, spawn_blocking discipline. Chunking reuses it unchanged.
  • Atomic note ingest (corpus.rs/store.rs): memory_ingest embeds each note whole; idempotent stable ids. Correct for short notes; there is no document chunking anywhere — the gap §9 fills.
  • Streaming chat loop (gen_ui_agent::chat): OpenAI-shaped streaming with tool-call accumulation across chunks. It currently assembles context inline; after this spec it requests an assembled context from the builder.

Gaps this spec closes: no capability profiles; no budget arithmetic anywhere; no chunking; no MMR/recency re-ranking; no history strategies; Android tool calling now targets LiteRT-LM constrained decoding/manual tools rather than llama.cpp llguidance; no context telemetry.

S07-008 · 5. Architecture

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5. Architecture

S07-009 · 5.1 Crate placement

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5.1 Crate placement

New workspace crate gen_ui_context (Rust, no engine deps, no_std-clean core not required but wasm32-clean is):

gen_ui_types ──► gen_ui_context ──► consumed by: gen_ui_agent, gen_ui_host,
                     │                gen_ui_server_axum, gen_ui_ffi,
                     │                gen_ui_wasm, tauri-plugin-gen-ui
                     ├── depends on: gen_ui_db_graph (retrieval traits only)
                     └── never depends on: gen_ui_inference engines

Capability inversion holds: gen_ui_context knows about budgets and retrieval capabilities through traits; it never links an inference engine, and no engine crate links it. gen_ui_agent asks the builder for an AssembledContext; the builder asks injected providers (history store, memory store, KB store, tool registry, token estimator) for slices. Compile-time dependency direction is the guarantee, per the standing Fabric invariant.

6.2 ModelProfile — what the weights can do

pub struct ModelProfile {

    pub family: String,

    pub trusted_context: u32,           // 8_192 — empirically defended ceiling

}

trusted_context is the load-bearing field: it is set by the Phase 0 needle test (§14, P0-3), not copied from a model card. nominal_context exists only so the UI can explain the difference to a curious user.

S07-016 · 6.4 SessionEnvelope — the measured layer

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.4 SessionEnvelope — the measured layer

Mutable per-session state the resolver consults on every turn:

pub struct SessionEnvelope {
    pub consecutive_inferences: u32,
    pub session_infer_ms: u64,
    pub thermal_state: ThermalState,    // Nominal | Warm | Hot (OS-reported where available)
    pub last_ttft_ms: Option<u64>,
    pub last_total_tokens: Option<u32>, // feeds PreCompactPolicy (fork parity)
}

Envelope rules (deterministic, tunable per DeviceProfile): after max_consecutive_inferences (default 12 mobile) or thermal_state == Hot, the resolver downgrades — shorter output reserve, fewer RAG chunks, then recommends cloud handoff via a typed EscalationAdvice the host surfaces. This encodes §3.5 as mechanism instead of hope.

S07-017 · 6.5 TokenEstimator

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.5 TokenEstimator

trait TokenEstimator { fn estimate(&self, text: &str) -> u32; fn kind(&self) -> EstimatorKind; } Implementations: ExactTokenizer (llama.cpp vocab via FFI on-device; HF tokenizer server-side), CharsHeuristic (chars/4, fork parity, web fallback). The plan records which estimator produced its numbers; safety margin widens from 10% → 15% when the heuristic is in play. Cross-platform consistency requires estimating with the model's own tokenizer wherever possible — Qwen3.5's 248K vocab tokenizes materially differently than chars/4 assumes.

S07-018 · 6.6 Resolution

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.6 Resolution

pub fn resolve(
    device: &DeviceProfile,
    model: &ModelProfile,
    runtime: &RuntimeProfile,
    envelope: &SessionEnvelope,
    overrides: &BudgetOverrides,        // user/agent/session layered, fork-style
) -> EffectiveCapabilities

Order: preset lookup (device×model) → derivation rules (§7.2) → envelope degradation → override merge (only tightening overrides accepted from non-privileged layers, mirroring the Cedar posture: product supplies defaults, users may tighten). Result is cached per (profiles, envelope-bucket) and logged once per session for reproducibility.

S07-019 · 7. Budget abstraction

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7. Budget abstraction

S07-020 · 7.1 BudgetPlan — the contract every platform honors

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.1 BudgetPlan — the contract every platform honors

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BudgetPlan {
    pub context_ceiling: u32,           // = trusted_context unless extended flag

    // Token slices (hard caps)
    pub system_prompt_max: u32,
    pub tool_schema_max: u32,
    pub history_max: u32,
    pub memory_max: u32,                // user memories slice
    pub knowledge_max: u32,             // dropped-notes / KB RAG slice
    pub output_reserve: u32,
    pub thinking_reserve: u32,          // 0 when thinking disabled this turn
    pub safety_margin_pct: u8,          // 10 exact-tokenizer / 15 heuristic

    // Item-count caps (independent of tokens)
    pub max_tool_shortlist: u8,         // tools exposed to one call
    pub max_memory_items: u8,
    pub max_kb_retrievals: u8,          // chunks after re-ranking
    pub max_history_messages: Option<u16>,

    // Retrieval tuning
    pub chunk_target_tokens: u16,       // 250–400 band
    pub rerank: RerankPlan,             // §10
    pub placement: PlacementPolicy,     // §10.3

    // Agentic caps (§3.4)
    pub max_autonomous_steps: u8,       // before checkpoint
    pub mutating_action_gate: GatePolicy, // AlwaysConfirm (non-negotiable default)
}

S07-021 · 7.2 Derivation rules

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.2 Derivation rules

Given C = context_ceiling after safety margin:

  1. output_reserve and thinking_reserve come off the top (never squeezed).
  2. system_prompt_max + tool_schema_max are fixed by tier.
  3. history_max fixed by tier; strategy (§8) keeps history inside it.
  4. memory_max + knowledge_max = remainder, split by tier ratio (default 30/70 — dropped notes are the larger corpus; memories are short).
  5. Invariant checked at resolve time: Σ slices + margin ≤ C — violation is a config error, not a runtime clamp.

S07-022 · 7.3 Named tier presets (initial values)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.3 Named tier presets (initial values)

Numbers for the two mobile tiers carry over from the budget analysis earlier in this design cycle; cloud/desktop are set generously but still finite — consistency of shape across platforms is the product requirement.

Field mobile-4b (S25U) mobile-9b (iPhone 17 PM) desktop-local web-wasm cloud-server
context_ceiling 8 192 8 192 16 384 8 192 32 768¹
system_prompt_max 500 600 1 200 600 2 000
tool_schema_max 200 300 800 300 1 500
history_max 1 200 1 800 4 000 1 800 8 000
memory_max 600 850 1 800 850 3 000
knowledge_max 1 400 1 950 4 200 1 950 7 000
output_reserve 768 1 024 2 048 1 024 4 096
thinking_reserve (when on) 512 768 1 536 512 4 096
safety_margin_pct 10 10 10 15 10
max_tool_shortlist 4 6 8 5 8
max_memory_items 3 4 6 4 8
max_kb_retrievals 3 5 8 5 10
chunk_target_tokens 250 320 400 320 400
max_autonomous_steps 3 4 6 3 8

¹ Cloud ceiling is per-model via liter-llm metadata; 32K is the floor preset. Thinking reserve is carved from output+knowledge when toggled on for a turn — the resolver emits a per-turn variant plan, so "thinking on" visibly costs RAG chunks rather than silently overflowing.

S07-023 · 7.4 Enforcement — the BudgetLedger

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.4 Enforcement — the BudgetLedger

Assembly runs against a BudgetLedger that debits each slice as content is admitted. Policies per slice: Hard (refuse and record), Shrink (drop lowest-ranked items first — retrieval slices), Summarize (history slice, strategy-mediated). Overflow at final render is a defect: the ledger makes it unreachable by construction, and a debug assertion + telemetry counter back that claim in CI and in the field.

S07-024 · 8. Context-management strategies (fork port, budget-aware)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8. Context-management strategies (fork port, budget-aware)

S07-025 · 8.1 Trait and resolver

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.1 Trait and resolver

#[async_trait]
pub trait ContextStrategy: Send + Sync {
    fn kind(&self) -> StrategyKind; // None|SlidingWindow|TruncateMiddle|Summarize|Hierarchical
    async fn apply(
        &self,
        history: Vec<Turn>,
        cfg: &StrategyConfig,
        ledger: &mut BudgetLedger,   // history slice only
        cx: &StrategyCx<'_>,         // estimator, summarizer handle, persisted metadata
    ) -> Result<StrategyOutcome, ContextError>;
}

pub struct StrategyOutcome {
    pub turns: Vec<Turn>,
    pub summary_updated: Option<SummaryRecord>,
    pub facts_extracted: Vec<FactRecord>,
    pub removed: u32,
    pub tokens_saved: u32,
    pub was_applied: bool,
}

StrategyResolver reproduces the fork's layered merge exactly: defaults → global settings → assistant/agent config → topic/session override, key-by-key, with hasOverride semantics preserved so a partial override doesn't clobber unrelated fields. Agent sessions default to None + explicit opt-in, as in the fork. The hygiene filter chain (context-clear, empty, error-pair, adjacent-user, user-role-start) runs before any strategy, ported as pure functions with the fork's tests translated to Rust.

S07-026 · 8.2 SlidingWindow

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.2 SlidingWindow

Token-budget-first (the fork's "dynamic" mode becomes the primary mode): admit turns newest→oldest until history_max or max_history_messages is hit; maxMessages remains as an optional cap for fork parity. Never splits a turn; never separates a tool call from its result (a constraint the fork handles upstream via filters — here it is a builder invariant).

S07-027 · 8.3 TruncateMiddle

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.3 TruncateMiddle

keep_first (default 2) + keep_last (default 4) with an explicit omission marker turn ([… N earlier messages omitted …]) when show_omission_marker. Marker text is part of the token math, not free.

S07-028 · 8.4 Summarize (progressive)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.4 Summarize (progressive)

Real implementation, not fallback. Trigger: history over history_max AND turn count ≥ summarize_threshold (6). The oldest overflow block is summarized into ≤ summary_max_tokens (500) by a summarizer route: on-device it reuses the loaded model with a short constrained prompt at temp 0.2 (one extra inference — the SessionEnvelope charges it); cloud/desktop may route to a designated small model (fork's summarizationModelId). SummaryRecord persists (SurrealDB, §11.3) with the covered turn-ids so re-summarization is incremental — fork's summarizedMessageIds parity. Failure mode honored: if the summarizer call fails or the envelope forbids the extra inference, degrade to SlidingWindow for this turn and record it in telemetry; never block the user's message on a summary.

S07-029 · 8.5 Hierarchical (three-tier) — the KnowMe-native strategy

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.5 Hierarchical (three-tier) — the KnowMe-native strategy

Short-term: last short_term_turns (5) verbatim. Mid-term: rolling summary inside mid_term_summary_tokens (2000 desktop/cloud; clamped to the history slice on mobile). Long-term: extracted durable facts within long_term_facts_tokens (500). The KnowMe twist: long-term facts are not a parallel store — extraction writes them through the existing memory ingest (gen_ui_db_graph::memory_ingest, kind "fact", provenance = session id), so hierarchical memory and user memories converge on one governed store and facts become retrievable by the same RRF pipeline in future sessions. This is the mechanism that makes "it knows the user" compound over time. Extraction is opt-in per assistant and surfaced in the UI (sovereignty: users see what was written and can delete it; deletion respects the standing memory-removal path).

S07-030 · 8.6 PreCompactPolicy (agent/cloud lane)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.6 PreCompactPolicy (agent/cloud lane)

Fork parity: cache the prior turn's total-token usage; when it exceeds compact_trigger_tokens, run a compaction step (strategy-mediated summarize) before dispatching the next user message. On-device this maps to "force-summarize now"; on cloud SDK sessions it maps to the provider compact primitive where one exists.

S07-031 · 9. Chunking subsystem

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

9. Chunking subsystem

S07-032 · 9.1 Router

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

9.1 Router

Content entering the knowledge path is routed by size and structure:

Condition Strategy Notes
≤ 1.5 × chunk_target_tokens Atomic Current memory_ingest path unchanged — short notes stay whole
Prose above threshold SemanticBoundary Split on paragraph/heading boundaries near target size; never mid-sentence
Unstructured / very long RecursiveOverlap Size-targeted splits with 10–15% overlap
Long docs where precision matters ParentChild Embed child chunks (target size); store parent window reference; inject parent context at assembly

S07-033 · 9.2 Data model

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

9.2 Data model

pub struct ChunkRecord {
    pub id: String,                  // stable: {doc_id}#c{ordinal}
    pub doc_id: String,
    pub ordinal: u32,
    pub text: String,
    pub token_len: u32,              // by the ingest-time estimator
    pub parent_span: Option<(u32, u32)>, // char range in parent for window fetch
    pub kind: String,                // extends MemoryRecord.kind: "chunk"
    pub source: ChunkProvenance,     // doc title, ingest ts, origin (dropped|scribe|fact)
}

SurrealDB (3.x strict syntax) additions live beside the existing memory table; chunks embed through the same Embedder (batch API, spawn_blocking), HNSW DIMENSION 384 unchanged. Ingest of an N-chunk doc is one transaction; re-ingest of the same doc_id replaces its chunk set (stable ids ⇒ idempotent, matching seed_corpus discipline).

S07-034 · 9.3 Injection

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

9.3 Injection

At assembly, a selected child chunk may be widened to its parent span if and only if the knowledge ledger can afford it; widening is ranked (best hit widens first). Provenance flows into ContentBlock::Citation/Memory so the UI can show which note grounded an answer — a sovereignty feature, not just debugging.

S07-035 · 10. Retrieval & re-ranking pipeline

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10. Retrieval & re-ranking pipeline

S07-036 · 10.1 Stages

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.1 Stages

query ──► lanes (vector | BM25 | graph-hop)      [existing gen_ui_db_graph]
      ──► RRF fuse (k=60, limit=20)              [existing, unchanged]
      ──► MMR diversity pass (λ default 0.7)     [new — embedding math only]
      ──► recency boost: score × exp(−λr·age_d)  [new — λr per corpus kind]
      ──► truncate to max_kb_retrievals / max_memory_items
      ──► optional parent widening (§9.3)
      ──► placement (§10.3)

MMR uses the vectors already fetched for the RRF candidates — zero extra model calls, bounded O(k²) at k ≤ 20. Recency defaults: memories λr = 0.01/day (gentle), facts 0.005, chunks 0 unless the doc kind opts in. Both passes are pure functions with property tests.

S07-037 · 10.2 Memory vs knowledge lanes

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.2 Memory vs knowledge lanes

Memories and knowledge chunks are retrieved as separate pipeline runs against separate ledger slices (memory_max / knowledge_max). One shared run would let a large dropped document starve the user's explicit memories — the exact inversion of the product promise.

S07-038 · 10.3 PlacementPolicy

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.3 PlacementPolicy

Per §3.3: rank-1 item is placed last in its section (adjacent to the user query); rank-2 first; remaining ranks fill the middle. Sections order: system → tools → long-term facts → history → memories → knowledge → query. Placement is deterministic and covered by golden tests: same inputs, same bytes.

S07-039 · 10.4 Cross-encoder gate (deferred)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.4 Cross-encoder gate (deferred)

Add a reranker model only if, after MMR+recency ship, retrieval precision is still the measured bottleneck (eval set: ≥50 real query/expected-note pairs; precision@3 target 0.8). If added: runs over RRF top-15–20 only, desktop/cloud first; mobile only if the envelope affords it. Until that gate, the extra forward passes buy less than they cost on-device.

S07-040 · 11. Assembly pipeline & data models

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

11. Assembly pipeline & data models

S07-041 · 11.1 End-to-end turn sequence

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

11.1 End-to-end turn sequence

1  resolve EffectiveCapabilities (profiles + envelope + overrides)   [cached]
2  derive per-turn BudgetPlan variant (thinking on/off, degraded?)
3  tool stage: registry → relevance shortlist (≤ max_tool_shortlist)
      → minimal one-line descriptions in-prompt
      → full schemas compiled to grammar (llguidance) once per session
4  history stage: hygiene filters → resolved ContextStrategy.apply(ledger)
5  memory stage: retrieval pipeline against memory_max slice
6  knowledge stage: retrieval pipeline against knowledge_max slice (+widening)
7  assemble: PlacementPolicy orders sections; ledger proves Σ ≤ ceiling
8  render: engine-neutral PromptPlan → engine adapter maps to chat template
9  generate (structured turns: grammar-constrained, temp ≤ 0.2)
10 post: semantic validation → ≤2 repair retries → fail closed
11 telemetry event; envelope update; PreCompactPolicy check for next turn

Steps 1–8 are synchronous, deterministic, engine-free. Only 3 (grammar compile) and 4 (summarize path) may incur model work, both envelope-charged.

S07-042 · 11.2 Core assembly types

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

11.2 Core assembly types

pub struct AssembleRequest {
    pub user_turn: Turn,
    pub session_id: String,
    pub assistant_id: String,
    pub thinking_requested: bool,
    pub overrides: BudgetOverrides,
}

pub struct AssembledContext {
    pub plan: BudgetPlan,               // the variant actually used
    pub prompt: PromptPlan,             // ordered sections, engine-neutral
    pub tool_shortlist: Vec<ToolRef>,
    pub grammar: Option<GrammarHandle>,
    pub telemetry: ContextTelemetryEvent,
    pub escalation: Option<EscalationAdvice>,
}

pub struct PromptPlan {
    pub sections: Vec<Section>,         // (SectionKind, Vec<RenderedItem>)
    pub estimated_tokens: u32,
    pub estimator: EstimatorKind,
}

PromptPlan is the cross-platform contract: Dart/TS mirrors are generated (flutter_rust_bridge / ts-rs) so every UI can display exactly what will be sent — the transparency surface the sovereignty story requires.

S07-043 · 11.3 SurrealDB additions (3.x strict)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

11.3 SurrealDB additions (3.x strict)

DEFINE TABLE chunk SCHEMAFULL;
DEFINE FIELD doc_id     ON chunk TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD ordinal    ON chunk TYPE int;
DEFINE FIELD text       ON chunk TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD token_len  ON chunk TYPE int;
DEFINE FIELD kind       ON chunk TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD provenance ON chunk TYPE object;
DEFINE FIELD embedding  ON chunk TYPE array<float>;
DEFINE INDEX chunk_hnsw ON chunk FIELDS embedding HNSW DIMENSION 384;

DEFINE TABLE context_summary SCHEMAFULL;   -- SummaryRecord (fork TopicContextMetadata parity)
DEFINE FIELD session_id  ON context_summary TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD text        ON context_summary TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD covered_ids ON context_summary TYPE array<string>;
DEFINE FIELD updated_at  ON context_summary TYPE datetime;

DEFINE TABLE context_turn_log SCHEMAFULL;  -- telemetry ring (bounded, local-only)
DEFINE FIELD session_id ON context_turn_log TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD event      ON context_turn_log TYPE object;
DEFINE FIELD at         ON context_turn_log TYPE datetime;

Writes use type::record($table, $key) and two-arg UPDATE form per standing SurrealDB 3.x discipline; no id field inside content objects. Facts from §8.5 go to the existing memory table (kind "fact"), not a new table.

S07-044 · 12. Telemetry & consistency guarantees

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

12. Telemetry & consistency guarantees

ContextTelemetryEvent (Rust mirror of the fork payload, extended): strategy_kind, tokens_before, tokens_after, tokens_saved, messages_removed, slices: Vec<(SliceKind, budget, spent, items)>, estimator, degraded: bool, escalation: Option<…>, trigger. Emitted on the AG-UI stream (agui.* namespace) so any surface can render a context inspector; persisted to the bounded local ring only. Guarantees the fabric makes testable: (G1) byte-deterministic assembly; (G2) ledger-proven no-overflow; (G3) tool call/result pairing never split; (G4) mutating-action gate cannot be disabled by non-privileged override layers; (G5) memory slice cannot be starved by knowledge slice.

S07-045 · 13. Failure scenarios & trade-offs (what hurts)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

13. Failure scenarios & trade-offs (what hurts)

Per standing discipline, the scenarios that hurt this design, named:

  1. Token-estimation drift. chars/4 on Qwen3.5's 248K vocab can misestimate by 20–30% on code/multilingual text; even the exact tokenizer path costs an FFI round-trip per slice. Mitigation is the widened margin + estimator telemetry, but a systematic underestimate still means silent quality loss near the ceiling. Residual risk: medium until P0-2 measures real drift.
  2. Summarization on-device is an extra inference. It competes with the thermal envelope and adds latency exactly when conversations are longest. The degrade-to-sliding-window path caps the damage but means the summarize strategy silently behaves like sliding window on hot devices — users may perceive memory loss. Telemetry makes it visible; it does not make it free.
  3. GDN × Q4 interaction is uncharacterized. If the P0-3 needle test shows retrieval breaking below 8K on either GGUF, every tier table in §7.3 shrinks and the product's on-device RAG story narrows. Probability subjectively 20–35%; impact contained because trusted_context is a data field, not a constant.
  4. Two token vocabularies of truth. Fork-era chats managed by chars/4 and fabric-era chats managed by exact counts will window differently; users migrating desktop→mobile may see different history depth. Accepted; documented in release notes rather than papered over.
  5. Preset ossification. Hardcoded tier numbers rot as models/devices change. Mitigation: presets are data files versioned with the app + overridable server-side for cloud tier; the needle test is rerun per new GGUF as a release gate.
  6. The scenario that hurts Prometheus: a competitor ships "just use the cloud" with a 200K window and no budget UX, and it feels smarter on day one. Our counter is compounding personal memory (§8.5) + sovereignty + consistency — but that is a bet on retention economics, not an immediate demo win, and it should be stated as such to stakeholders.

S07-046 · 14. Project plan

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

14. Project plan

Phases gate on KDD discipline: each ends in a reviewable artifact + explicit approval before the next begins. Estimates are ranges at stated confidence; they assume one primary implementer with review support.

Phase 0 — Spikes & gates (3–5 days, 80% confidence) - P0-1: Wire LiteRT-LM Android SDK constrained decoding/manual tool calling on Android; keep iOS Qwen/Metal as a separate re-certification lane. Gate: Android CPU baseline produces valid bounded tool calls before GPU/NPU optimization. - P0-2: Estimator drift measurement — exact tokenizer vs chars/4 over a 50-doc corpus (notes, code, mixed-language). Gate: margin table confirmed. - P0-3: Needle-in-haystack on actual Q4_K_M GGUFs (facts at 10/40/70/95% depth × 4K/8K/16K, both devices). Gate: trusted_context values set from data. - P0-4: SessionEnvelope thermal probe feasibility per OS (thermal state APIs on iOS/Android; fallback = inference-count-only).

Phase 1 — gen_ui_context core: capabilities + budgets (1.5–2.5 wks, 75%) Profiles, presets, resolver, BudgetPlan/Ledger, TokenEstimator impls, golden tests. Exit: G1/G2 proven in CI; presets reviewed against P0 data.

Phase 2 — Strategies + assembly (2–3 wks, 70%) Hygiene filters, four strategies (summarize/hierarchical real), resolver layering with fork tests ported, PromptPlan render, telemetry event. Exit: fork-parity test suite green; gen_ui_agent::chat consumes the builder behind a feature flag.

Phase 3 — Chunking + retrieval upgrades (1.5–2 wks, 75%) Chunk router/strategies, SurrealDB schema, MMR + recency passes, placement, memory/knowledge slice separation, citation provenance to ContentBlock. Exit: precision@3 eval harness exists with baseline numbers recorded.

Phase 4 — Platform adapters (1–2 wks, 70%) FFI surface (flutter_rust_bridge), Tauri command, wasm build, Axum middleware; preset loading + envelope probes per platform. Exit: same golden assembly bytes on all four targets in CI.

Phase 5 — Field hardening (1–1.5 wks, 60%) Context inspector UI hook-up, degraded-mode UX, PreCompactPolicy on cloud lane, telemetry ring bounds, release-gate automation for P0-3 reruns.

Critical path: P0-3 → §7.3 numbers → everything. Total: 7–11 weeks. Explicitly out: cross-encoder (gated, §10.4), tool-calling LoRA.

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

S25-001 · Provider & Model Configuration Strategy

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Provider & Model Configuration Strategy

Scope: how KnowMe configures LLM/embedding providers and models across three resolution levels — global defaults, agent/assistant (client- or server-side), and conversation — plus embedding-model management for RAG indexes (knowledge bases, karpathy wikis, logs, loops) and usage-driven suggestions.

Status: v1.0 strategy, 2026-07-18. Companion to docs/strategies/local-models/README.md (acquisition, library UX) and docs/knowme-builder-extensibility-spec.md (settings scopes/sync). Studied against Cherry Studio, which handles this unusually well; we adopt its load-bearing ideas and diverge where KnowMe's multi-device sovereignty changes the problem.

S25-002 · 1. What Cherry Studio gets right (and what we adopt)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

1. What Cherry Studio gets right (and what we adopt)

From the Cherry Studio default-models docs, chat docs, and the model-configuration internals:

  1. Role-slot defaults, not one global model. Separate defaults for the default assistant model, a fast model for background chores (topic naming, keyword extraction), and a translation model — "the models used by the behind-the-scenes helpers," explicitly distinct from the chat model. Adopt, with more roles (§3).
  2. Assistant = role, Topic = conversation with that role. The assistant pins the system prompt, model, and sampling params; topics inherit; any topic can override; @-mention temporarily borrows another model for one reply while keeping context; an auto-reset policy decides whether new topics revert to the assistant's model or inherit the last override. Adopt all four behaviors verbatim (§4).
  3. Deterministic model identity: providerId::modelId. One key format everywhere (their user_model table), with per-model capabilities, userOverrides, and orderKey. Adopt — it is exactly what our entity graph and OFP sync want (§2).
  4. Capability tags with a resolution precedence. vision / function-calling / reasoning / embedding / rerank per model; resolved as registry-force → user overrides → registry add/remove, so user removals survive registry updates. Adopt precedence unchanged (§2.3).
  5. Provider-specific settings are schema, not special-cased UI (Azure api-version, Vertex project, custom OpenAI-compatible base URLs). Adopt via our settings-schema renderer (§2.2) — one generic form engine, per-provider schemas.

Where we must diverge: Cherry Studio is a single-machine app. KnowMe's config must survive multiple devices with different local capabilities plus shared peers — that changes identity, resolution, and sync (§5).

S25-003 · 2. The registry

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2. The registry

S25-004 · 2.1 Providers

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.1 Providers

{
  "id": "prov-anthropic",             // stable, user-scoped
  "kind": "anthropic",                 // local-engine | bossfang | anthropic | openai |
                                       // openai-compatible | ollama | azure-openai | vertex | …
  "label": "Anthropic",
  "base_url": null,                    // overridable where kind allows
  "auth_ref": "keychain://prov-anthropic",  // secrets NEVER in the settings doc —
                                       // OS keychain via Tauri secure storage / Flint Vault server-side
  "settings": { /* validated by the provider-kind's JSON Schema */ },
  "health": { "state": "ok", "checked_at": "…", "latency_ms": 240 }
}

Two provider kinds are KnowMe-specific and auto-registered, never hand-configured:

  • local-engine — the in-process llama.cpp/mistral.rs runtime; its model list is the local model library (local-models §12). Exists on every device; contents differ per device.
  • bossfang — one provider per connected instance from Settings → Instances, created/removed with the instance itself. Its model list is served by the peer (the cyan remote rows in the moodboard). Health = OFP reachability.

Cloud kinds route through liter-llm in UAR — the vendored submodule (rust/vendor/universal-agent-runtime v1.0.0) carries a 269-provider catalog as discovery data (a catalog entry is not execution certification; provider access stays capability- and health-gated) — but are presented as first-class providers with their own rows, keys, and health checks. Every provider row: status dot · label · base host · kind pill · "Check" button (connectivity + auth + a 1-token echo), matching the moodboard Providers tab.

S25-005 · 2.2 Provider-kind schemas

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.2 Provider-kind schemas

Each kind ships a JSON-Schema for its settings (api-version for Azure, project/region for Vertex, org id for OpenAI, TLS options for custom). The generic schema→form renderer from the extensibility spec draws the UI; adding a provider kind (including via a .pxt extension exporting a provider capability) never requires new settings UI code. This is how we stay "Cherry-class" on provider coverage without their hand-built per-provider screens.

S25-006 · 2.3 Models

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2.3 Models

Key: provider_id::model_id (adopted). Record: capability set (chat, vision, tools, reasoning, embedding, rerank), context length, pricing (cloud) or size/quant + measured tok/s (local, from the benchmark gate), enabled, order_key, user overrides. Capability resolution: registry force → user overrides → registry add/remove (adopted). The registry layer is fed by: the signed KnowMe catalog (local models), the provider's /models listing (cloud), and the peer's advertisement (bossfang). Users can hand-add models a provider doesn't list (custom deployments).

S25-007 · 3. Global level — role slots

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3. Global level — role slots

Cherry Studio's insight, extended. Global settings bind roles to model refs:

Role slot Used by Default guidance
chat.default New assistants/conversations without a pin The §10 device recommendation (local)
utility.fast Topic naming, summarization, memory extraction, digest drafting, karpathy log/loop summarization Small + cheap + local: Qwen3 1.7–4B class
agent.default New Hands without an explicit model Tool-calling floor for the tier (14B+/MoE, or a peer)
vision.default Ask Image, image drops in chat Gemma E-class / 3 4B+
translation One-click translate Any chat model; user preference
embedding.default Seed for new indexes only (§6 — never applied retroactively) EmbeddingGemma@768 (device-appropriate)
rerank.default Optional second retrieval stage Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B, desktop/server only

Rules: every slot shows provenance and fallback ("local Qwen3 8B; falls back to BossFang home-mac when unloaded"). Role slots are user-scoped settings — they sync via the CRDT settings layer — but a slot bound to a local-engine model resolves per-device (§5). The utility.fast slot is what keeps background chores (Cherry's "behind-the-scenes helpers") off the expensive model — same separation, more consumers: Hands digests, memory writes, wiki/log/loop maintenance all draw from it.

S25-008 · 4. Agent and conversation levels

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4. Agent and conversation levels

S25-009 · 4.1 Agent/assistant level

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.1 Agent/assistant level

An assistant (chat persona) or Hand pins: model_ref (or "inherit global"), sampling params (temperature, top-p, max tokens, ctx), and — for Hands — the deployment target, which scopes resolution: a Hand deployed to home-mac resolves its model against that instance's providers at run time, not the authoring device's. This is the client-side/server-side split the FUNC-SPEC's Hands wizard (Step 2 Model, Step 3 Deployment) already sketches; the registry makes it precise: the wizard's model picker filters to capabilities ⊇ tools and the chosen target's available models, and warns when a pick is below the tool-calling floor for that target's hardware.

S25-010 · 4.2 Conversation level

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.2 Conversation level

Adopted from Cherry Studio wholesale, in moodboard terms:

  • The model chip at the top of Chat (already in Screen 02) is the per-conversation override: tap → selector grouped by provider, capability-filtered, with fit/trust pills carried over from the library. An override is sticky for that conversation and labeled with provenance: "Qwen3-14B — set for this conversation."
  • @-mention in the composer borrows a model for a single reply with full context ("Mention model" behavior) — including multiple mentions for side-by-side answers; the transcript records which model produced which message (per-message model attribution is already implied by the moodboard's per-message thinking blocks).
  • Auto-reset policy (per assistant, default ON): new conversations revert to the assistant's model; OFF inherits the last override. Exposed as one toggle, phrased in outcomes: "New conversations start with this assistant's model."

S25-011 · 4.3 Resolution order (the whole system in six lines)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.3 Resolution order (the whole system in six lines)

message-level  @mention            (one reply)
  → conversation override          (sticky, this topic)
    → assistant/Hand pin           (+ params; Hands: scoped to deployment target)
      → role slot                  (chat.default / agent.default / …)
        → device recommendation    (local-models §10, if the slot is unset)
          → ask the user           (never silently pick a cloud provider)

Every level may be unset; the effective choice always renders its source. One hard rule from the sovereignty posture: resolution never escalates locality on its own — a chain that resolves to a local model may fall back to a peer, but falling back to a cloud provider requires an existing Cedar grant for that provider, or a prompt.

S25-012 · 5. Multi-device semantics (where we go beyond Cherry Studio)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5. Multi-device semantics (where we go beyond Cherry Studio)

A pinned local-engine model may not exist on the next device. Resolution therefore has a placement walk when the bound ref is unavailable here:

  1. Same model_id on a reachable bossfang provider → use it (chip shows cyan remote);
  2. Same catalog equivalence class locally (the signed catalog groups e.g. Qwen3 {4B, 8B, 14B} as tier-variants of one family; pick the device-appropriate tier and label it "device equivalent");
  3. Offer: download it here (jumps into the local-models §2 flow) / pick another / use peer.

Sync scopes (per the extensibility-spec settings model): role slots and assistant pins are user-scoped (CRDT-synced); the placement of local-engine refs and anything bound to device hardware is device-scoped; provider auth is secret (keychain, never CRDT — each device holds its own copy; BossFang instances may hold shared keys in Flint Vault). Conversation overrides travel with the conversation entity through normal OFP sync, and the placement walk re-runs on whatever device opens it.

S25-013 · 6. Embedding models — per-index bindings, not a global knob

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6. Embedding models — per-index bindings, not a global knob

The embedding.default slot only seeds creation flows. The binding that matters lives on the index, because vectors are only comparable within one model+dim (local-models §11):

// stamped on every KB / karpathy wiki / log index / loop memory at creation
{
  "index_id": "kb-client-acme",
  "embedding": { "model_ref": "prov-local::embeddinggemma-300m", "dim": 256 },
  "rerank":    { "model_ref": null },
  "chunking":  { "strategy": "semantic", "target_tokens": 480, "overlap": 64 },
  "created_at": "…"
}
  • Immutable after creation except through an explicit re-embed migration: a visible job (progress, cancellable, old index kept until the new one completes) — the honest version of what most tools hide. Cherry Studio binds the embedding model at KB creation for the same reason; we make the migration path first-class instead of impossible.
  • Creation wizard: defaults from embedding.default, shows dim choice with the tradeoff stated ("256-dim: ~3× smaller/faster, slight recall cost — recommended on this device"), warns when the chosen model can't run on devices that sync this index ("your phone can embed queries with EmbeddingGemma but not BGE-M3 — queries will route to a peer").
  • Karpathy wikis / logs / loops (the karpathy-progress-memory artifacts): each gets the same binding block. Their maintenance passes (summarize, distill, link) draw from utility.fast; their retrieval uses the index's own embedding binding; loops that grade/reflect may pin a reasoning-capable model explicitly — that pin is an agent-level setting on the loop's Hand, resolved like any other (§4.1).
  • Mismatch on sync = re-embed job, never merge (restated from local-models §11); the index's {model_ref, dim} stamp is the guard.
  • Server-side indexes (flint-forge/BossFang corpus): may bind heavier models (BGE-M3 hybrid) and optionally embed in-database via Flint Ember; devices keep a device-appropriate binding over their hot subset. Two indexes, two bindings, one query plan — the read path merges results, it does not pretend the vectors are comparable.

S25-014 · 7. Usage-based suggestions

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7. Usage-based suggestions

All signals are local-only (SurrealDB; no analytics pipeline — FUNC-SPEC §09), the engine is rules over counters, and every suggestion is a dismissible card that explains itself and applies with one tap — never an automatic switch.

Tracked per (context, model_ref): use counts and recency; measured latency/tok/s; error and malformed-tool-call rates; regenerate-with-a-different-model events (the strongest preference signal: the user tried A, redid it with B); manual override frequency per assistant/topic-class; token spend per cloud provider (priced from the registry) vs. local; provider health history.

The cards these rules produce:

  • "In coding conversations you switch to Qwen3-Coder 8 of the last 10 times — make it the Coding assistant's model?"
  • "Inbox Triage has an 18 % malformed-tool-call rate on Qwen3-4B. Its target home-mac can run 30B-A3B at ~40 t/s — redeploy?" (agent-level, ties §4.1 to the tool-calling floor)
  • "This month: $14.20 to Anthropic for summarization tasks your local utility.fast model handles within quality thresholds — route utility tasks local?"
  • "Provider Groq failed 40 % of requests this week — health-check or disable?"
  • "Phi-4-mini hasn't been used in 90 days — reclaim 2.3 GB?"
  • After a benchmark: "Measured 47 t/s on the new model — 2.1× faster than your current chat default with equal capability tags. Swap?"

Suggestion cards land in the Models tile and (for agent-level ones) on the Hand's detail card, in the moodboard's cyan-annotation style: claim, evidence, one action.
